<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 13"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magitaxis](/Feats.aspx?ID=5396) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Surki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=789" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 51

**Prerequisites**
[Vestigial Magicsense](/Feats.aspx?ID=5388)

**Trigger**
A creature you could reach with a Stride action Casts a Spell from the tradition matching your magiphage ability.

</column>

---

You move reflexively toward the source of magic you most consumed as a larva. You Stride, and you must end your movement adjacent to the triggering creature. You then can't use Magitaxis against the triggering creature for 24 hours as your reflexes reacclimate, though you can use it against other creatures.

 You can use Magitaxis while [Burrowing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Striding (changing the trigger accordingly) if you have the corresponding movement type.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magnetic Field](/Feats.aspx?ID=4255) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 30

</column>

---

A magnetic field surrounds you. Choose a polarity when you take this action. You can switch the polarity as a free action at the start of each of your turns while you remain in this stance.

 **Attract** A creature that is wearing metal armor, has the metal trait, or is made of metal treats squares in your kinetic aura as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) when moving away from you. You pull unattended metal objects of light Bulk or less in your kinetic aura to you. They gather in your space and move with you.

 **Repel** A creature that is wearing metal armor, has the metal trait, or is made of metal treats squares in your kinetic aura as difficult terrain when moving closer to you. You push unattended metal objects of light Bulk or less in your kinetic aura away. They stop moving once they're outside your aura.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magnetic Pinions](/Feats.aspx?ID=4252) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=540" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 30

</column>

---

Small pieces of metal fly from you, propelled with magnetism at great velocity. Make ranged impulse attack rolls against up to three creatures within 60 feet of you; you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your attack roll against any target wearing metal armor or made of metal. All three attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but it doesn't increase until after all the attacks. The metal pieces deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage and 1d4 piercing damage on a hit (or double damage on a critical hit).

---
**Level (+2)** Each type of damage increases by 1d4.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magpie Manor Recovery](/Feats.aspx?ID=8873) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 47

**Archetype** [Dandy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=246)

**Prerequisites**
[Dandy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6302)

</column>

---

Though you're hardly ready to retire from the social life, you appreciate the luxury the older wealthy elite enjoy within the private social club of Magpie Manor in Absalom's Petal District. And you try to bring that luxury even to the wilds of the world. If you have a four-person tent and spend at least 10 minutes setting it up to your level of comfort before taking an 8-hour period of rest, you regain an additional number Hit Points equal to double your level and reduce the severity of your [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition by 2 instead of 1. Up to three other Medium or smaller creatures can share the tent with you and gain these benefits.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magus Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2945) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 75

**Archetype** [Magus](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=95)

**Prerequisites**
Strength 14 or Dexterity 14; Intelligence 14

</column>

---

You cast spells like a magus, gaining a [spellbook](/Equipment.aspx?ID=53) with four common [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) cantrips of your choice. You gain the Cast a Spell activity. You can prepare two cantrips each day from your spellbook. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new level from the magus archetype, add a spell of that level or lower to your spellbook. You're trained in arcane spell attack rolls and spell DCs. Your key spellcasting ability for magus archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are arcane magus spells. You become trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2); if you were already trained in Arcana, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in simple weapons.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the magus archetype.

<title level="2">Magus Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Magus Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=2950), [Basic Martial Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=2946), [Hybrid Study Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2947), [Spellstriker](/Feats.aspx?ID=2948)

You announce your name to your enemies, bringing your constellation to bear in a blinding display. Attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) all enemies within 30 feet. Demoralize loses the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait and gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait when used this way. In addition to the regular effects of Demoralize, enemies become [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 minute on a successful check (and also blinded for 1 round on a critical success).

You can use Majestic Proclamation as a single action if your previous action was Starlit Transformation.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Mammoth Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3443) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #177: Burning Tundra](/Sources.aspx?ID=116) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Mammoth Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=170)

**Prerequisites**
[Ride](/Feats.aspx?ID=835)

</column>

---

You've undertaken the ultimate challenge of the Mammoth Lords and tamed a megafauna. You gain a megafauna you tamed as a [young animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=151). Your megafauna animal companion must be a megafauna appropriate to the Realm of the Mammoth Lords; see the What Counts as Megafauna? sidebar for guidance and examples. While an animal companion usually starts as Small, you can begin with a Medium version of that animal (changing no statistics other than its size).

 Contrary to the usual rules for animal companions, this feat can give you a second animal companion. If you have more than one animal companion, you can adventure with only one of them at a time. You can switch between them like a [beastmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=50) does. You gain the Call Companion action, as the beastmaster archetype, and you follow all the other rules found in the Call Companion sidebar.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from this archetype.

<title level="2">Mammoth Lord Dedication leads to...</title>
[Gigantic Megafauna Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3452), [Mammoth Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3444), [Mature Megafauna Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3445), [Megafauna Veterinarian](/Feats.aspx?ID=3446), [Specialized Megafauna Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3453), [Speech of the Mammoth Lords](/Feats.aspx?ID=3447), [Staggering Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=3450), [Stalwart Mind](/Feats.aspx?ID=3449), [Unbreakable Bond](/Feats.aspx?ID=3451)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 111

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

**Prerequisites**
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320)

</column>

---

Thanks to your continued belief in your ultimate transformation, you have learned greater control over your manifested realm. If you spend a Mythic Point when you Manifest your Realm, you can use the Drain Realm, Spread Realm, and Unleash Realm free actions.

 **Drain Realm** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** Your previous action was to Sustain your manifested realm; **Requirements** Your manifested realm has a radius of at least 10 feet; Effect You siphon power from your manifested realm to bolster your physical form. Decrease your manifested realm's radius by 10 feet. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to your level and each of your Strikes made before the end of your turn deal an additional 1d8 damage of your realm's damage type.

 **Spread Realm** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** Your previous action was to Sustain your manifested realm; **Effect** Your manifested realm further corrupts more of your surroundings. Increase your manifested realm's radius by 10 feet.

 **Unleash Realm** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** Your previous action was to Sustain your manifested realm; **Effect** You punish those who transgress upon your realm. An enemy within your realm takes 4d8 damage of your realm's damage type with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

Against [humanoids](/Traits.aspx?ID=91), you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47), and to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) and [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50).

 Once per day, you can cast [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34) as a divine innate spell using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Casting it requires staring into the target's eyes, giving the spell the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait. At 5th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the spell is heightened by an additional level, to a maximum of a 9th-level charm when you are 19th level.

<title level="2">Manipulative Charm leads to...</title>
[Dominating Gaze](/Feats.aspx?ID=3556)

[Many Faces](/Feats.aspx?ID=6940) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 68

**Frequency**
three times per day

**Prerequisites**
[Everyday Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6930)

</column>

---

Putting on a new face offers a great way to get a fresh perspective on life. When you Change Shape into your everyday form, you gain the effects of a 3rd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) for 1 hour or until you shift back, whichever comes first, except it’s a [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect rather than an [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629). However, your transformations can be broken with a good shock; if you gain the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) condition while transformed, your transformation ends, returning you to your tanuki form, and your confidence is so shaken you can’t attempt to resume that specific disguise again until your next daily preparations.

>
[Many Guises](/Feats.aspx?ID=2091) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 197

**Archetype** [Vigilante](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=80)

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5); [Vigilante Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2083)

</column>

---

You can take on any number of mundane guises. Whenever you change your identity, instead of taking on your social or vigilante identity, you can become someone completely ordinary. This identity isn't a specific individual—rather, you become a nondescript member of your ancestry, of any gender, with a neutral alignment and a mundane occupation such as common laborer, farmer, or peasant. Spells and abilities detect you as if you were this ordinary identity, rather than either of your two real identities, unless they succeed at a counteract check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC. You can't use either social abilities or vigilante abilities while in this identity.

You’re as skilled in combat underwater as on land. You gain the [Underwater Marauder](/Feats.aspx?ID=5230) skill feat, and when you roll a success on an Athletics check to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381), you get a critical success instead. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 41

**Usage**
imbued into a worn ikon

</column>

---

Your ikon gains a pin, stripe, or similar marking showing you as a master of your craft. The imbued ikon gains the following ability. 

**Transcendence—A Challenge for Heroes** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (concentrate, mental, spirit, transcendence) You declare an enemy within 60 feet to be a heroic test. For 1 minute, that enemy deals an additional 10 spirit damage to you with each successful Strike or spell it targets you with. Whenever that enemy deals spirit damage to you, each ally who has the enemy in melee reach can attempt a [Reactive Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2256) against it, even if the ally doesn’t normally have that reaction. If an ally successfully slays the enemy with a Reactive Strike due to this effect, that ally immediately gains temporary Hit Points equal to your level, which persist for 1 minute.

---

You've combined your social skills and combat training to become a talented combat leader. Choose [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7). You become trained in that skill or become an expert if you were already trained in it.

 In addition, you're surrounded by a marshal's aura in a 10-foot emanation. Your aura has the [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), and [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) traits and grants you and allies within the aura a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68).

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the marshal archetype.

Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) or Trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40); trained in martial weapons

</column>

---

You’ve combined your social skills and combat training to become a talented combat leader. Choose [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40). You become trained in that skill or become an expert if you were already trained in it.

In addition, while you’re conscious, you’re surrounded by a marshal’s aura in a 15-foot emanation. Your aura has the [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), and [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) traits and grants you and allies in the aura a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598).

[Back to Back](/Feats.aspx?ID=6358), [Cadence Call](/Feats.aspx?ID=6356), [Coordinated Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=6361), [Dread Marshal Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=6352), [Form Up!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7018), [General's Gambit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7019), [Inspiring Marshal Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=6353), [Know Your Enemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=7017), [Rallying Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=6357), [Snap Out of It!](/Feats.aspx?ID=6354), [Steel Yourself!](/Feats.aspx?ID=6355), [Strategist Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7016), [Tactical Cadence](/Feats.aspx?ID=6362), [Target of Opportunity](/Feats.aspx?ID=6363), [To Battle!](/Feats.aspx?ID=6359), [Topple Foe](/Feats.aspx?ID=6360)

[Marshall Fiendish Forces](/Feats.aspx?ID=7324) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

**Prerequisites**
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320)

</column>

---

You have been in contact with a retinue of [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), brokering all manner of deals so that they may eventually serve you. When you [Manifest your Realm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2986), you can choose to have one such fiend come to your aid. This fiend is a [common](/Traits.aspx?ID=557) fiend of level 11 or lower, which you select when you take this feat. The fiend appears in a place of your choosing within your manifested realm and has the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait. They remain for as long as your realm is manifested, until they’re reduced to 0 Hit Points, or until you command them to leave, at which point they immediately vanish and return to their place of origin. 

At 20th level, you can choose a common fiend of level 15 or lower to appear instead when you Manifest your Realm.

---

You have trained to use your fists as deadly weapons. The damage die for your fist unarmed attacks becomes 1d6 instead of 1d4. You don't take the –2 circumstance penalty for making a lethal attack with your [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) unarmed attacks. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain that proficiency rank in all unarmed attacks.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the martial artist archetype.

<title level="2">Martial Artist Dedication leads to...</title>

**Archetype** [Warrior Of Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=286)

**Trigger**
A creature attacks your bonded partner.

**Requirements**
You are wielding a weapon that has the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait, and your bonded partner is within reach of one of your melee Strikes with that weapon.

</column>

---

You intercede to absorb the triggering attack. Your bonded partner gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mask Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=1103) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 101

**Archetype** [Magaambyan Attendant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=29)

**Prerequisites**
[Magaambyan Attendant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1102)

</column>

---

Your mask takes on a personality of its own, allowing it to serve as your [familiar](/Familiars.aspx). Though you can still wear it as a mask, you can detach it from your face to grant it a bodily form of colored light that allows it to move around; usually, this is a miniature form of the animal the mask represents. Detaching or reattaching the familiar to transform it is a two-action activity. Even in mask form, the familiar can move around on its master’s face and speaks in a distinct voice (if it can talk). It is easily recognized as more than a simple mask unless the familiar succeeds at a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) a mask. Other than its appearance and the fact that it can be worn, it functions as other familiars. Your mask familiar has access to the mask freeze familiar ability

**Mask Freeze**: When in mask form, your familiar can hide its obvious supernatural qualities to pass as a simple, unassuming mask. It doesn’t need to Impersonate to fool a passing glance, and it gains a +4 circumstance bonus to its Deception DC against an active observer [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) or otherwise studying it.

<title level="2">Mask Familiar leads to...</title>
[Adaptive Mask Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=1104), [Crusader's Masquerade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7758)

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Trigger**
You start your turn with the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) condition.

**Requirements**

---

Your _warmask_ burns off of your face, releasing your apprehension. You remove the frightened condition. Your _warmask_ is destroyed, and you can't reapply it until your next daily preparations.

**Special** You can use this free action even if you have a condition tied to the frightened condition that would normally prevent you from using a free action, such as “[fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=17) as long as you're frightened” or “[paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28) as long as you're frightened.”

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mask of The 12th Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7568) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 291

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566); Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)

</column>

---

You have reached the 12th Step and been instructed in greater secrets of [Razmir’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) doctrine. You can [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593) out of [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920) or upgrade your existing mask to a silver one in the same time it takes to Craft one made of iron . A silver Razmiri mask grants a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), is a 10th-level item, and gains the following activation in addition to that possessed by the standard mask.

**Activate—Call Upon Razmir’s Mercy** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** Exhorting Razmir to purge impurities from your target, you lay hands on a creature within reach and cast [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) as an [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell with a spell rank equal to half your level. Unlike a normal _cleanse affliction_ spell, this doesn’t reduce the stage of the affliction; instead, if the counteract check is successful, the [affliction’s](/Rules.aspx?ID=2389) stage is temporarily reduced by 1 and its effects are suppressed for 24 hours, after which the affliction resumes in full force. If the target would have been required to attempt additional saves against the affliction during the 24 hours it was suppressed, they must attempt all of those saving throws as soon as the 24-hour duration ends. This could mean that the target saves successfully and it is as if the affliction were truly healed, or it could mean that the affliction returns and advances multiple stages all at once.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Masquerade of Seasons Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=4044) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=19" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 126

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

You have mastered the opening steps to the Masquerade of Seasons, a dance that channels the power of spring, summer, winter, and autumn. Choose one of the following traits: [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118), or [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27). You gain resistance 5 to damage dealt by effects with the chosen trait. You can use an action to reenter this stance at any time, changing the granted resistance to another of the available options. If you are at least 12th level, the granted resistance increases to be equal to half your level.

<title level="2">Masquerade of Seasons Stance leads to...</title>
[Grand Dance](/Feats.aspx?ID=4046), [Pirouette](/Feats.aspx?ID=4045)

---

Kalistrade teaches that setbacks are only temporary and that perseverance is a treasured virtue. When you fail, but not critically fail, at a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) or Mercantile [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) check to Earn Income at a specific task and are allowed to continue working at that task on subsequent days, you can choose to attempt the skill check again the next day. If you succeed, you get a critical success and continue to earn that amount on further days spent working at the task, if the task lasts that long.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Master's Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2247) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The trigger for Master’s Counterspell should begin with “A creature Casts a Spell that you have prepared or is in your repertoire...” to provide a trigger for spontaneous spellcasters as well as prepared spellcasters._

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134); master in spell attack rolls and spell DCs

**Trigger**
A creature Casts a Spell that you have prepared, and that spell was cast or created with a tradition of magic in which you have master proficiency in spell attack rolls and spell DCs.

</column>

---

When a foe Casts a Spell and you can see its manifestations, you can use your magic to disrupt it. If you're a prepared caster, you can expend a prepared spell to counter the triggering creature's casting of a spell. If you're a spontaneous caster, you can expend a spell slot. The level of the prepared spell or spell slot must be at least as high as the triggering spell's level. You lose your prepared spell or spell slot as if you had Cast the Spell. You then attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the triggering spell, and you take a –2 penalty to your counteract check; for prepared casters, the GM might waive the penalty if the spell you're expending to counterspell is especially appropriate—such as countering with the same spell, or using a [_cone of cold_](/Spells.aspx?ID=47) to counteract a [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Masterful Obfuscation](/Feats.aspx?ID=2238) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 44

**Archetype** [Scrollmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=31)

**Prerequisites**
master in a skill with the [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) action; [Scrollmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1130)

</column>

---

You've mastered the art of deceiving others about your area of study. When you gain this feat, choose one skill with the [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) action in which you have attained master proficiency. You can attempt to deceive others about the truth of facts and knowledge related to that skill—such as by pretending to know something that you don't, planting false information, or the like—using the [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) action of the [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) skill. When you Lie in this way, attempt your skill check using the skill you selected when you gained this feat instead of Deception, applying all bonuses or penalties related from the selected skill to the check. While it's easier to convince someone who knows nothing about your chosen false information, on a critical success, you can even convince someone who has heard something contradictory, unless they have reason to be certain from direct experience. For instance, you might say, “I know you may have heard to use [silver weapons](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) against [vampires](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=97), but that's a misconception based on conflating them with [werewolves](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=100). According to all credible scholars, [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) will do the trick.” Once a creature realizes you've used masterful obfuscation to Lie to them, either from a failed check or due to later discovering the falsehood, you can't use this feat against them again, as it relies on blind trust in your superior knowledge. However, you can still Lie to them normally.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 39 **Usage** imbued in one or two weapon ikons that both have the [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=711) trait --- Your ikons bond like a pair of one-winged birds. This feat can be imbued in either a single ikon with multiple copies, such as one produced by the shadow sheath or with the [Twin Stars](/Feats.aspx?ID=7156) feat, or two separate ikons (bypassing the normal limit per ikon feat). **Immanence** As long as you hold one ikon, the other will return to find its partner. Both ikons gain the [returning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2845) rune.
**Transcendence—Rejoin in Flight** (transcendence) You throw your weapon ikons to either side of a creature, and they seek each other out, converging on the target. Make two thrown Strikes against a target within the first range increment of both your weapon ikons. This counts as two attacks toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both attacks. The target is flanked for both attacks (typically making it off guard against both attacks). If both Strikes hit, the target also takes an additional die of weapon damage. The weapons then return to your hand.

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 130

**Archetypes** [Rivethun Involutionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=310) (Level 6), [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381) (Level 6)

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Your animal companion has grown up over the course of your adventures, becoming a mature animal companion and gaining [additional capabilities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2117).

Your animal companion has greater independence. During an encounter, even if you don't use the Command an Animal action, your animal companion can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Strike or Stride (or Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim if it has that Speed). It can do this at any point during your turn, as long as you aren’t currently taking an action. If it does, that’s all the actions it gets that round—you can’t Command it later.

You specialize in weapons that require two hands. You become trained in all simple and martial melee weapons that require two hands to wield or have the [two-hand](/Traits.aspx?ID=198) trait. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in weapons, you also gain that proficiency rank in these weapons. If you are at least an expert in such a weapon, you gain access to the critical specialization effect with that weapon.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the mauler archetype.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 53

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), Legendary in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Legendary in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or Legendary in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

You can trap a foe in a twisting, extradimensional labyrinth of ever-shifting runes. You can cast [_quandary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1644) once per day as an [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232). The rank of this spell is equal to half your level rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least legendary in the related skill. Instead of the usual skill checks to solve the puzzle, the target of your _quandary_ can attempt a [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) check, a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363), or a check in the skill related to the tradition of the spell. When you [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this spell, you can also [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) or [Invoke one Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4265) on the target creature as if it were adjacent to you.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 139 --- You open yourself to the guidance of whatever spirits or powers deign to help you. Roll 1d4 to see what type of spirit is drawn to you. Your next action must be the type of action the spirit prefers, but you also gain the listed benefit for the action as the spirit guides you. If you attempt to use a different action, you must succeed at a DC 6 flat check or the action is lost.
**1 Warrior** You must attempt a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306). You gain a +1 status bonus to your attack roll and a +2 status bonus to damage, or a +6 status bonus to damage if you are at least [cursebound](/Traits.aspx?ID=800) 3.
**2 Adept** You must attempt a Perception check or a skill action. You gain a +1 status bonus to the check, or a +2 status bonus if you are cursebound 3.
**3 Sage** You must attempt to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734). You gain a status bonus to the spell's damage or healing equal to the spell's rank, or equal to the spell's rank + 3 if you are at least cursebound 3.
**4 Wanderer** You must attempt a [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) action, or a [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), or [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) action if you have the relevant speed. You gain a +10- foot status bonus to your Speed for the action, or a +20-foot status bonus if you are at least cursebound 3.

---

You become an expert in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9). When you succeed with [Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=760) or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57), the target regains 5 additional HP at DC 20, 10 HP at DC 30, or 15 HP at DC 40. Once per day, you can use Battle Medicine on a creature that's temporarily immune. If you're a master in Medicine, you can do so once per hour.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you gain two other feats from the medic archetype.

[Doctor's Visitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=2028), [Preventative Treatment](/Feats.aspx?ID=3618), [Resuscitate](/Feats.aspx?ID=2031), [Treat Condition](/Feats.aspx?ID=2029)

Kassi has taught you not only how to apply medicines with your medical skills but how to craft them as well. <title level="2">Kassi's Techniques</title>

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 71

While Kassi shares her greatest discoveries with the entire medical community, some of her techniques are either still experimental or extremely difficult to perform. Any students who Kassi takes on gain access to her techniques.

**Related Feats**: [Paragon Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=2171)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mega Bomb](/Feats.aspx?ID=128) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Additive 3" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=4" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 81

**Prerequisites**
[Expanded Splash](/Feats.aspx?ID=109)

**Requirements**
You are holding an infused alchemical bomb you crafted, with a level at least 3 lower than your advanced alchemy level.

</column>

---

You add an incredibly powerful additive to a held bomb to create a mega bomb, greatly increasing its area and power. You use an Interact action to throw the mega bomb, rather than Strike, and you don’t make an attack roll. The mega bomb affects creatures in a 30-foot-radius burst, centered within 60 feet of you. The bomb deals damage as if each creature were the primary target, with a basic Reflex save. On a failed save, a creature also takes any extra effects that affect a primary target (such as flat-footed from [bottled lightning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=76)). While all targets in the area take splash damage as primary targets, there is no further splash beyond that area. If your next action after creating a mega bomb isn’t an Interact action to throw it, the mega bomb denatures and loses all effects.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 69

</column>

---

You can add a highly explosive additive to an alchemical bomb to turn it into a mega bomb. Throwing this bomb takes a 2-action activity instead of a Strike. This isn't a Strike, and you don't make an attack roll. The mega bomb explodes in a 30-foot burst within 60 feet. It deals damage as if each creature were the primary target, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. On a failed save, a creature also takes any extra effects that affect a primary target (such as [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) from [bottled lightning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3290)). Though all targets in the area take [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage as primary targets, there is no further splash beyond that area.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Megafauna Veterinarian](/Feats.aspx?ID=3446) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #177: Burning Tundra](/Sources.aspx?ID=116) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Mammoth Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=170)

**Prerequisites**
[Mammoth Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3443); Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)

</column>

---

By heeding the wise advice of elders in your following— and aided by your own experience—you've learned how to provide medical care to the megafauna of the Mammoth Lord followings. You can attempt a [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) check instead of a [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) check for any of Medicine's trained and untrained uses, provided the subject of your medical care is a megafauna. If you're attempting an action that requires a particular proficiency rank in Medicine (such as [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57)), use your proficiency rank in Nature instead. If the subject of your care is your megafauna and you roll a success on your check, you get a critical success instead.

    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Megavolt](/Feats.aspx?ID=3062) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Electricity" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=56" />
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 27

</column>

---

You bleed off some electric power from your innovation in the shape of a damaging bolt. Creatures in a 20-foot line from your innovation take 3d4 electricity damage, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. The electricity damage increases by 1d4 at 8th level and every 2 levels thereafter.

 **Unstable Function** You overload and supercharge the voltage even higher. Add the [unstable](/Traits.aspx?ID=416) trait to Megavolt. The area increases to a 60-foot line and the damage increases from d4s to d12s.

 If you have the breakthrough innovation class feature, you can choose a 60-foot or 90-foot line for the area when you use an unstable Megavolt; if you also have the revolutionary innovation class feature, you can choose a 60-foot, 90-foot, or 120-foot line.

**Special** If your innovation is a [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109), it can take this action rather than you.

<title level="2">Megavolt leads to...</title>
[Gigavolt](/Feats.aspx?ID=3076)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Meld into Eidolon](/Feats.aspx?ID=2892) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Summoner" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=392" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 67

</column>

---

Your physical form can combine with that of your eidolon, granting benefits but limiting your capabilities. You [Manifest your Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757), but instead of summoning it into an adjacent open space, you become it. While Manifested in this way, you use its statistics, and you can't act except to direct it to use Manifest an Eidolon to unmanifest it. Since you can't act, you can't Cast Spells, activate or benefit from magic items that normally benefit you and not your eidolon, perform actions that have the [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) trait, or use other abilities that require you, and not the eidolon, to act. Your can't be separately targeted while you are melded into it. When you reach 0 HP, your eidolon unmanifests, leaving your body behind, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11). You can Meld Into Eidolon while your eidolon is already manifested as long as it's adjacent to you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Meld Into Eidolon](/Feats.aspx?ID=9227) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Summoner" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=954" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 78

</column>

---

Your physical form can combine with that of your eidolon. You Manifest your Eidolon, but instead of summoning them into an adjacent open space, you become them. You can also Meld into Eidolon while your eidolon is manifested in an adjacent space. While Manifested in this way, you use your eidolon’s statistics, and you can’t act except to direct the eidolon to use Manifest an Eidolon to unmanifest themself. Your eidolon is affected by [_boost eidolon_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1045) while Manifested in this way.

Since you can’t act, you can’t cast spells, activate or benefit from magic items that normally benefit you and not your eidolon, perform actions that have the [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) trait, or use other abilities that require you, and not the eidolon, to act. You can’t be separately targeted while you are melded into the eidolon. When you reach 0 HP, your eidolon unmanifests, leaving your body behind, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) and [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69).

If your Performance check is successful against an observer’s Perception DC, that observer doesn’t notice that you are Casting a Spell, even though normally spells have sensory manifestations that would make spellcasting obvious to those around you, and verbal, somatic, and material components are extremely overt. You hide all of these as part of an ordinary performance.

 This hides only the spell’s spellcasting actions and manifestations, not its effects, so an observer might still see a ray streak out from you or see you vanish.

You subtly weave your spellcasting into a performance. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=72), the spell gains the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait, hiding the shining runes, sparks of magic, and other manifestations that would usually give away your spellcasting. The trait hides only the spell’s spellcasting actions and manifestations, not its effects, so an observer might still see a ray streak out from you or see you vanish into thin air.

As part of using Melodious Spell, you can choose to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387), [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395), [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=2401), or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393). If you do so, the spell you cast must have the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697), or [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait to gain the subtle trait.

Your years of training in a previous life didn’t go to waste with your death, and you can call upon this training when you most need it. Choose one skill. </column>

---

Your spells release soothing mental waves. Use this amp in place of a psi cantrip's normal amp entry. You can use this amp only on a psi cantrip that targets or affects you or one or more of your allies and doesn't target or affect any enemies.

---
**Amp** You or one ally within 30 feet gains a +2 status bonus to Will saves against emotion effects for 1 minute. You can also have the amped psi cantrip attempt to counteract one effect imposing the frightened condition on yourself or the chosen ally, or an effect imposing the stupefied condition that has a duration of 1 hour or less. If you successfully counteract the effect, you remove only the frightened and stupefied conditions, not any other part of the effect.

>
[Mercenary Motivation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7691) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Blackjacket](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=316)

**Prerequisites**
[Blackjacket Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7689)

</column>

---

A large part of being in the Mercenary League entails doing mercenary work. You spend 1 minute planning a course of action that will allow you to complete a task you’ve been hired or requested to do. Work with your GM to determine the circumstances of any job or task if need be, but typically, they can involve protecting a place or person, defeating a foe or enemy force, or retrieving an item. The course of action you plan must be something you believe you can accomplish.

**Active Plan** You can have only one course of action planned at a time. If you use Mercenary Motivation to plan a second course of action, you no longer receive the bonus to checks related to the first course of action.

**On the Job** Whenever you attempt a [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) check or skill check that will advance your course of action, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the check. The exact checks this bonus applies to depend on your current job and are determined by the GM.

**Finishing a Plan** When you complete the course of action you planned to do, you don’t lose the bonus or other benefits until you make a different plan with Mercenary Motivation or voluntarily [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the current plan.

<title level="2">Mercenary Motivation leads to...</title>
[Close Contract](/Feats.aspx?ID=7695), [Nothing Personal](/Feats.aspx?ID=7694)

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 35 **Requirements** You and your allies are currently outnumbered by enemies on the battlefield. --- Even though the fight seems to be surging against you and your compatriots, you know that a key ally can always turn the tide. Choose a target you are currently observing. You assail it with a list of reasons why it should join you and why its defeat if it does not is surely inevitable. The target attempts a Will save against your class DC with the following results.
**Critical Success** The target is uninterested in joining you and is temporarily immune to further uses of this ability for 24 hours.
**Success** The target is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1 as it is forced to consider the merits of your offer.
**Failure** The target swaps sides and joins you for the duration of the battle. It gains the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) condition, but it can attempt a Will save whenever it takes damage or whenever you direct it to take an action that goes against its nature. On a success, the effect ends and it rejoins its former allies.
**Critical Failure** As a failure, but the target is so impressed by your leadership that it thanks you for the privilege of fighting alongside you; if it is still alive at the end of combat, it turns over any coins, wealth or other monetary possessions it has as tribute.

**Prerequisites**
[_lay on hands_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2047)

</column>

---

Your touch soothes the body or mind. You can cast [_lay on hands_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2047) targeting a living creature using 2 actions instead of 1. If you do, you can attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) one condition of your choice affecting the target. When you select this feat, choose one of the following options, which determines the conditions you can choose: **Mercy of the Body** [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59), [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65), [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91); **Mercy of Grace** [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61), [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85); **Mercy of the Mind** [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74), [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76), [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94).

**Special** You can select this feat up to three times. Each time, choose a different type of mercy and add its options to those you can choose when you cast a 2-action _lay on hands_.

[Affliction Mercy](/Feats.aspx?ID=5912), [Blessed Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=6279), [Greater Mercy](/Feats.aspx?ID=5904), [Ultimate Mercy](/Feats.aspx?ID=5929)

fields.text: Feat 4 Mercy Champion Source Player Core 2 pg. 95 Archetypes Blessed One (Level 6), Blessed One (Level 6) Prerequisites lay on hands Your touch soothes the body or mind. You can cast lay on hands targeting a living creature using 2 actions instead of 1. If you do, you can attempt to counteract one condition of your choice affecting the target. When you select this feat, choose one of the following options, which determines the conditions you can choose: Mercy of the Body blinded, dazzled, deafened, enfeebled, sickened; Mercy of Grace clumsy, grabbed, paralyzed; Mercy of the Mind fleeing, frightened, stupefied. Special You can select this feat up to three times. Each time, choose a different type of mercy and add its options to those you can choose when you cast a 2-action lay on hands . Mercy leads to... Affliction Mercy, Blessed Spell, Greater Mercy, Ultimate Mercy

    right="Feat 1"

[Merfolk Weapon Familiarity](/Feats.aspx?ID=5344) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Merfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=761" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 36

</column>

---

You were taught the most effective weapons of the sea. You gain access to all uncommon weapons with the [merfolk](/Traits.aspx?ID=761) trait. You have familiarity with [crossbows](/Weapons.aspx?ID=425), [heavy crossbows](/Weapons.aspx?ID=428), [longspears](/Weapons.aspx?ID=361), [spears](/Weapons.aspx?ID=365), and [tridents](/Weapons.aspx?ID=401)—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

 At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its [critical specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=235).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 166

**Archetype** [Celebrity](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=54)

**Prerequisites**
[Celebrity Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1931)

</column>

---

When you meet someone's gaze, they are unable to look away. Choose one target creature. That creature must succeed at a Will save or be [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) until the end of your next turn; the DC for this save is equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. If the creature succeeds at its save or its fascination ends due to a hostile action, it becomes temporarily immune to your Mesmerizing Gaze for 1 day.

When you select this feat, it gains either the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11) or [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) trait; once you make this choice, you can't change it.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Metal Carapace](/Feats.aspx?ID=4253) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 30

</column>

---

Sheets of bent and rusted metal cover you in an armored shell. The carapace is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency. The carapace's statistics are: _AC Bonus_ +3; _Dex Cap_ +2; _Check Penalty_ –2; _Speed Penalty_ –5 feet; _Strength_ +2; _Bulk_ 2; _Group_ [plate](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=4); _Armor Traits_ [noisy](/Traits.aspx?ID=205). Any bonuses, runes, and magical abilities of your actual armor are suppressed, but any that could apply to the metal carapace are replicated onto it.

 When you use this impulse, you can also create a rusty steel shield in a free hand, which uses the statistics of a regular [steel shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19). You can [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) with this shield even if you don't have that feat. The hand wielding this shield counts as a free hand for using impulses. The shield crumbles to flakes of rust if it becomes [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2) or leaves your grasp.

 The impulse lasts for 10 minutes, and you can Dismiss this impulse. If you use this impulse again, any existing one ends. The metal is rusted and fragile. If you take damage from a critical hit, the metal shatters and the impulse ends.

---
**Level (+3)** The shield's Hardness increases by 1, its HP by 4, and its BT by 2.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Mind Smith](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=194)

**Prerequisites**
[Mind Smith Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3862)

</column>

---

You have learned to stretch your mind's influence further, releasing projectiles with a swing of your mind weapon. You can make ranged mind weapon Strikes; these are ranged Strikes with a maximum range of 30 feet that deal 1d6 damage of the same type as your mind weapon. Your ranged mind weapon Strike gains all the benefits of your mind weapon's runes as long as they still apply to a ranged weapon. For example, if your weapon had _+1_, [_striking_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280), and [_spell-storing_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=305) runes, you would get a +1 item bonus to hit with your ranged mind weapon Strike, and it would deal the additional damage from the _striking_ rune, but it wouldn't be able to unleash a spell from the _spell-storing_ rune, as that rune can be etched onto only melee weapons.

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 204 **Archetype** [Mind Smith](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=194) --- You've learned to imagine a shape in your mind, to envision it so strongly it takes form in the material world. You gain a single melee weapon of your choosing, called a mind weapon. Your mind weapon is a martial melee weapon. The overall shape and design of your mind weapon can be of your choosing but it has one of the following four basic statistics:
  • A one-handed weapon that deals 1d4 damage and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) and [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) traits
  • A one-handed weapon that deals 1d6 damage and has the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) trait
  • A one-handed weapon that deals d8 damage
  • A two-handed weapon that deals 1d10 damage and has the [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) trait
Each day during your daily preparations, you can decide if you want your weapon to deal bludgeoning damage and be in the [club](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5) weapon group, deal piercing damage and be in the [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14) weapon group, or deal slashing damage and be in the [sword](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=15) weapon group. Your mind weapon is an extension of your mind—it has no Hardness, and any ability that would damage your mind weapon instead damages you directly, pushing back against the weapon's corporeal form and becoming mental damage of the same amount the weapon would have taken. You can project your mind weapon using an Interact action, just as you would draw any other weapon. Only you can hold, carry, or wield your mind weapon; if held by another person, it quickly disappears from their hand, reforming in your mind for you to project again. If you're disarmed of your mind weapon, it dematerializes, but you can draw it again with an Interact action starting at the beginning of your next turn. Upon creating your mind weapon, you also learn to use a mind smith's keepsake: an object of light Bulk, such as a bracelet or figurine, that you wear or keep on your person and inscribe with weapon runes. Your keepsake can't be a magic item, nor can it have any significant monetary value beyond the value of any runes you inscribe on it. You can buy and inscribe [fundamental runes](/Equipment.aspx?Category=23&Subcategory=25) and [weapon property](/Equipment.aspx?Category=23&Subcategory=27) runes onto your keepsake in the same way you would for a regular weapon, and you can move runes to and from your keepsake to other weapons or runestones for the usual cost. Any runes inscribed on the keepsake apply to your mind weapon when you create it. If your keepsake is ever lost or destroyed, you can spend 1 week of downtime imprinting a new object with your weapon's mental properties, though this new keepsake won't have any of the runes that were inscribed on the prior keepsake. **Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the mind smith archetype. Mind Smith Dedication leads to... [Ghost Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=3864), [Just the Tool](/Feats.aspx?ID=3865), [Malleable Movement](/Feats.aspx?ID=3863), [Mental Forge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3866), [Metallic Envisionment](/Feats.aspx?ID=3871), [Mind Projectiles](/Feats.aspx?ID=3869), [Mind Shards](/Feats.aspx?ID=3867), [Runic Mind Smithing](/Feats.aspx?ID=3870)

[Mindblank Mutagen](/Feats.aspx?ID=124) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 81

</column>

---

With a minor adjustment of ratios in the formula for your [serene mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=100), you gain mental protections. When you’re affected by a serene mutagen, [detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=43), [revelation](/Traits.aspx?ID=138), and [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=141) effects of 9th level or lower detect nothing from you or your possessions and auras. For instance, [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) would still detect other magic in the area, but not any magic on you.

Precious metals from your bloodstream line your claws, jaws, or the tip of your tail, and you’re able call upon your blood to surge and empower your attacks. ---

When you are in your social identity, you can also grant a social identity to an animal companion, familiar, or other minion you gained from a class feature. When changing to your social identity, you also change your minion's appearance to that of a socially acceptable creature of its type, such as grooming a wolf to appear as a large dog or disguising a familiar to appear as an exotic pet. Commanding your minion to use unusual magical or combat abilities it gained from your class features or feats while in this social identity risks exposing your vigilante identity.

Through divine intervention or whispered prayers, you foil an enemy's response. If the triggering creature's level is equal to or lower than yours, you disrupt the triggering reaction. fields.text: Feat 12 Miraculous Intervention Reaction Uncommon Champion Cleric Source Knights of Lastwall pg. 85 Access Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat. Trigger An adjacent fiend or undead begins to use a reaction. Through divine intervention or whispered prayers, you foil an enemy's response. If the triggering creature's level is equal to or lower than yours, you disrupt the triggering reaction. If the triggering creature's level is higher than yours, you must make an attack roll or spell attack roll against its AC (your choice). On a success, you disrupt the reaction.

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Miraculous Possibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1709) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 123

</column>

---

Your deity empowers you to perform minor miracles, allowing you to readily adapt to the fluctuating needs of your duties. Once during your daily preparations, you can use a spell slot to hold sheer divine potential, rather than using it to prepare a spell. You can use this spell slot to cast any spell you know from the divine spell list that's at least 2 levels lower than the slot you designate. The spell acts in all ways as a spell of 2 levels lower. You don't have any particular spell prepared in that slot until you cast it.

<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />

<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
<trait label="Undine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=314" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 31

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

Geniekin can't grant magical wishes, but some echo of power lingers within you. Faced with a mechanism that is damaged but not destroyed, you can wish it back into a functional state for a period of 10 minutes. The object must be mundane and no larger than 5 Bulk, such as a disabled locking mechanism in a door. For 10 minutes, the object functions as it should, ignoring any damage to its mechanism. This doesn't grant you any knowledge of what a device might do or how it ought to function. Once the 10 minutes are up, the object falls back into disrepair and is temporarily immune to Miraculous Repair for 1 day.

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Miresoul](/Feats.aspx?ID=2568) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lineage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=317" />
<trait label="Oread" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=304" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 106

</column>

---

You have a connection to the muddier denizens of the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=5) from its border with the [Plane of Water](/Planes.aspx?ID=7), and your elemental lineage manifests as clay or mud, reflecting that bond. Your body's mudlike quality makes it easy for you to compress and squeeze yourself through smaller areas. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1). If you would automatically become trained in Acrobatics (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the [Quick Squeeze](/Feats.aspx?ID=828) skill feat.

>
[Mirror Refuge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3801) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Reflection" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=431" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 121

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Mirror-Risen](/Feats.aspx?ID=3793)

**Requirements**
You're within 5 feet of a mirrored surface.

</column>

---

Your origin in the space behind mirrors enables you to use a mirror as a hideaway, like the spell [_meld into stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=188). You meld into an adjacent mirror. You can hear but not see outside this space, and creatures outside can't see or hear you. You can cast spells while within the mirror, but no effects can cross the mirror. Your Mirror Refuge lasts for 10 minutes unless the mirror is broken, which expels you and deals 10d6 damage to you. You can Dismiss the effect. You appear in a space adjacent to the mirror when the effect ends.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mirror Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=404) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 151

**Archetypes** [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=49) (Level 12), [Knight Vigilant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=27) (Level 12), [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=240) (Level 12)

**Trigger**
An opponent casting a spell that targets you critically fails a spell attack roll against your AC.

**Requirements**
You have a shield raised.

</column>

---

You reflect the spell back against the triggering opponent. Make a ranged attack against the triggering creature using your highest proficiency with a ranged weapon. If you can cast spells, you can make a spell attack roll instead. If you succeed, your opponent takes the effects of a successful spell attack roll for their own spell (or the effects of a critical success if your attack roll was a critical success).

<title level="2">Mirror Shield leads to...</title>
[Reflecting Riposte](/Feats.aspx?ID=1247)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 120

---

You were created from magic involving mirrors and still retain some ability to seek refuge in reflected illusions. You gain the Mirror's Trickery reaction. 

**Mirror's Trickery** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would be hit by a Strike; **Effect** You create an illusory duplicate at the last instant and attempt to trick your foe into striking it instead of you. The attacker attempts a DC 11 flat check; on a failure, the attack hits the duplicate, changing the result from a critical success to a success or a success to a failure.

<title level="2">Mirror-Risen leads to...</title>
[Mirror Refuge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3801), [Reflective Pocket](/Feats.aspx?ID=3798)

    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mist Escape](/Feats.aspx?ID=3555) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
[Turn to Mist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3553); [Coffin Bound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3554)

**Trigger**
You are reduced to 0 HP.

</column>

---

As you fall, your body reacts to defend itself. You Turn to Mist. This doesn't expend a use of Turn to Mist, and you can use Mist Escape even if you've already Turned to Mist in the same day. You take [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) actions to move directly toward your coffin even though you are at 0 HP, though you aren't conscious and don't have control over how you do so. While at 0 HP in this form, you are unaffected by further damage. You automatically return to your corporeal form, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), if you reach your coffin or after 1 hour when you are destroyed, whichever one comes first.

[Mobile Magical Combat](/Feats.aspx?ID=2248) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

You dart around the battlefield, casting spells while you carefully make melee attacks with your weapon. Stride once. If you end your movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, you can make a melee Strike against that enemy. You can use Mobile Magical Combat while [Burrowing](/Actions.aspx?ID=93), [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94), or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 35

</column>

---

Your thralls can now follow you wherever you go. Any thrall you create has your choice of a [climb Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2349) or [swim Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2351). The additional Speed is equal to its land Speed, and any time you let the thrall [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305), you can have it use the relevant movement action instead. 

At 8th level, add a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) to your choices. A flying thrall remains airborne at the end of your turn even if it didn’t [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) that turn.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 30

</column>

---

You are the relentless pursuer of your prey that nobody else can see. You can cast 4th-rank _invisibility_ as an occult innate spell once per day. When you cast _invisibility_ this way, you select one foe within line of sight. They can see you as if you weren’t [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), but they also take a –2 circumstance penalty to their Will saves and Will DC for as long as you are invisible and within their line of sight. If there is no foe within line of sight when you cast _invisibility_ this way, the spell fails.

You succeed at a check to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29) or use [Tumbling Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=1877), and you moved through an enemy's space.

The Mockingbird is a master at running into foes and coming away with their weapons. Mimicking their skill, you strike at a foe's wrist while tumbling past them, weakening their grip. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 53

**Archetype** [Sterling Dynamo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=110)

**Prerequisites**
[Sterling Dynamo Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3127)

</column>

---

Your dynamo has modular configurations, allowing you to swap between various different possibilities with ease in order to adapt to various situations in combat. Your dynamo attack gains the [modular](/Traits.aspx?ID=271) trait, as well as one of the following configurations of your choice: power driver (1d6 bludgeoning damage; [shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193)), percussive striker (1d4 bludgeoning damage; [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), rotating sickle (1d6 slashing damage; [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)), or entangling barbs (1d6 piercing damage; [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=184)). If you have a manually controlled dynamo, these damage dice increase by 1 size, as usual, and you can also choose the extendable baton (1d4 bludgeoning damage; [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), which has the damage increase already factored in.

 When you use an Interact action to switch configurations using the modular trait, you switch between the initial configuration of dynamo you chose with the Sterling Dynamo Dedication and the new configuration you chose with Modular Dynamo.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, you choose another configuration and add it to the list of options you can choose when you use an Interact action with the modular trait.

---

Spinning molten iron through a vortex of fire, you trap your foe in searing wires. Make an impulse attack roll against a creature within 15 feet. On a success, the target takes 2d6 slashing damage and is wrapped in molten wire for 1 minute. It is [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) and takes 2d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The wire's [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC is your class DC. The wire has AC 10 and 75 HP. The impulse ends if the creature Escapes or the wire is destroyed.

---
**Level (+4)** The slashing damage increases by 1d6, the fire damage increases by 1d4, and the wire's HP increases by 25.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 128

**Requirements**
You are unarmored and wielding a [longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=76), [shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=77), or a bow with the [monk](/Traits.aspx?ID=112) trait.

</column>

---

You enter a specialized stance for a unique martial art centered around the use of a bow. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are those using longbows, shortbows, or bows with the monk trait. You can use [Flurry of Blows](/Actions.aspx?ID=9) with these bows. You can use your other monk feats or monk abilities that normally require unarmed attacks with these bows when attacking within half the first range increment (normally 50 feet for a longbow and 30 feet for a shortbow), so long as the feat or ability doesn't require a single, specific Strike.

**Special** When you select this feat, you become trained in the longbow, shortbow, and any simple and martial bows with the monk trait. If you gain the expert strikes class feature, your proficiency rank for these weapons increases to expert, and if you gain the master strikes class feature, your proficiency rank for these weapons increases to master.

<title level="2">Monastic Archer Stance leads to...</title>
[Focused Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=1751), [Return Fire](/Feats.aspx?ID=1743), [Triangle Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=1761)

You have trained with the traditional weaponry of your monastery or school. You gain access to uncommon weapons that have the [monk](/Traits.aspx?ID=112) trait and become trained in simple and martial monk weapons. When your proficiency rank for unarmed attacks increases to expert or master, your proficiency rank for these weapons increases to expert or master as well.

Vanaras generally consider the spirits of departed monkeys to be less informative or interesting than their own ancestors traveling the cycles of existence, yet these monkey spirits can prove useful when the situation is dire. You can cast [_mad monkeys_](/Spells.aspx?ID=702) once per day as a 5th-level primal innate spell. You become an expert in primal spell DCs and primal spell attack rolls. If you choose flagrant burglary for this casting of mad monkeys, you can have the monkeys use your [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) modifier instead of your spell DC – 10.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Monster Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5180) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 258

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You can use the parts of monsters to aid in crafting. You can use the body of a monster to help Craft items, using Survival instead of Crafting for the Craft activity when you do so. If parts of the monster’s body are valuable, you can expend them toward the item’s raw material cost as well. (The GM makes the determination if the monster’s entry doesn’t list any valuable materials from its body.)

If you spend additional days working on the item, reduce the Price using the monster’s level instead of your own. Certain items may require specific creatures in their Craft requirement.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=682" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 157

**Archetype** [Bounty Hunter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=243) (Level 4)

</column>

---

You quickly assess your prey and apply what you know. As part of the action used to Hunt your Prey, you can attempt a check to Recall Knowledge about your prey. When you critically succeed at identifying your hunted prey with Recall Knowledge, you note a weakness in the creature’s defenses in addition to any other benefits. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll against that prey, and any ally you tell gains the same benefit. You can give bonuses from Monster Hunter only once per day against a particular creature.

Your attuned apparition grants Forest [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) or Ocean Lore as one of its apparition skills.

---

Your apparitions share with you the monstrous nature of those creatures who dwell in deep seas or ancient woods. You add [_monstrosity form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1608) to your apparition spell repertoire, allowing you to cast it with your apparition spellcasting.

**Special** If you are attuned to a stalker in darkened boughs, add the phoenix form from [_monstrosity form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1608) to your available [_darkened forest form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2143)  options when you cast the spell heightened to 8th rank.

If you are attuned to a lurker in devouring dark, add the cave worm and sea serpent forms to your [_devouring dark form _](/Spells.aspx?ID=2140) options as a [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect when you cast the spell heightened to 8th rank.

---

Your dual human and orc nature has given you a unique perspective, allowing you to bridge the gap between humans and the many intelligent creatures in the world that humans consider monsters. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks against non-humanoid intelligent creatures and against humanoids that are marginalized in human society (at the GM’s discretion, but typically at least including [giants](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=53), [goblins](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=55), [kobolds](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=65), and [orcs](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=80)). You also gain this bonus on [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=405) checks to [Sense the Motives](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) of such creatures.

Like the moray eels athamaru communities raise and train, you know how to quickly strike from hiding. Stride or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) directly toward the triggering creature and make a melee Strike against it. The target creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to this attack.

</traits>
