</column>

---

You have either trained a [giant moray eel](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2971) since its hatching or have tamed one in the wild. You gain the [Bonded Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=5127) skill feat, even if you don't meet the prerequisites, to bond with a giant moray eel. When you [Command this Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) while you are mounted on it to take a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action, you automatically succeed instead of needing to attempt a check.

**Special** If you have the [Elver Pet](/Feats.aspx?ID=5277) or [Growing Eel Friend](/Feats.aspx?ID=5282) ancestry feats, you can choose to have that pet become your bonded animal. You don’t need to spend 7 days of downtime to bond with the eel, and you automatically succeed at the [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) check. You can then [retrain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2634) those feats.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Reflection" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=431" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 120

</column>

---

You were once a shapeshifter or spellcaster using polymorph magic, but something went wrong, and you became trapped in the form of the creature you were imitating. This accident might have drained your power, or you might have retained some of your skills, but either way, your form resists further forced transformation. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157) effects, and if you roll a success on a saving throw against a hostile [morph](/Traits.aspx?ID=113) or [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) effect, you get a critical success instead.

<title level="2">Morph-Risen leads to...</title>
[Warp Likeness](/Feats.aspx?ID=3800)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Morphic Manipulation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3775) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Positive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=128" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 79

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)

</column>

---

You've attuned your natural aura to that of plant life, coaxing it to grow faster than normal. You sit for 10 minutes with a small, natural non-creature plant—such as a lone flower, a small bush, or a potted succulent—while you bring your aura in tune through meditation. You coax the plant to advance one stage in its life cycle: from seed to sprout, sprout to plant, plant to flower, or flower to fruit. If the plant doesn't have proper nutrients (if you're sprouting a seed without soil or water, for example), the plant withers 5 minutes after you complete the activity. Performing this activity more than once per day renders you [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) and unable to use Morphic Manipulation until your next full night's rest.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mortal Herald Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7528) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 279

**Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305)

**Prerequisites**
Worshiper of a specific deity; Master in [Religion or your deity’s divine skill](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

You become a mortal herald of your [deity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2048), gaining power in return for your service. Others intuitively sense your connection with your deity, which subtly influences the way they act around you. You become bound by your deity’s anathema. Depending on your deity, their sanctification can make you [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521). This gives you the holy or unholy trait, which commits you to one side of a struggle over the souls of the planes and can be referenced in other abilities. If you “can be” holy or unholy according to your deity, you make that choice, and if you “must be” holy or unholy you gain the trait automatically. If you gain the opposing trait in some way, you lose the previous trait until you complete an [atone](/Rituals.aspx?ID=108) ritual.

In addition, once per day, you can cast [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) as a 6th-rank innate divine spell. You can only target yourself with the spell, but you gain the benefits of the 2-action version when you spend 1 action to cast it. In addition, if you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not immediately killed, you can cast the spell as a free action before you become unconscious. This spell is automatically heightened to a rank equal to half your level.

**Special** If you have [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83), you instead cast [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1552).

<title level="2">Mortal Herald Dedication leads to...</title>
[Declare Anathema](/Feats.aspx?ID=7536), [Deific Font](/Feats.aspx?ID=7543), [Dive of the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=7537), [Divine Presence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7544), [Domain Embodiment](/Feats.aspx?ID=7529), [Ease the Burden](/Feats.aspx?ID=7551), [Enter Divine Realm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7552), [Eyes of God](/Feats.aspx?ID=7545), [Fear of God](/Feats.aspx?ID=7530), [Flash of Omipotence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7553), [Flash of Omnipresence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7531), [Flash of Omniscience](/Feats.aspx?ID=7546), [Glory on High](/Feats.aspx?ID=7547), [Guiding Words](/Feats.aspx?ID=7548), [Herald's Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=7532), [Heraldic Proclamation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7541), [Invisible Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=7542), [Marked For Rebuke](/Feats.aspx?ID=7549), [Moment of Apotheosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=7555), [Mortal Ascension](/Feats.aspx?ID=7533), [Shield the Faithful](/Feats.aspx?ID=7534), [Spark of Immortality](/Feats.aspx?ID=7556), [Stand for the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=7550)

You stomp, shaking the earth beneath you.     right="Feat 1"

>
[Mountain Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=435) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 159

**Archetypes** [Martial Artist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=67) (Level 4), [Martial Artist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=255) (Level 4)

**Requirements**
You are unarmored and touching the ground.

</column>

---

You enter the stance of an implacable mountain—a technique first discovered by dwarven monks—allowing you to strike with the weight of an avalanche. The only Strikes you can make are falling stone unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 bludgeoning damage; are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group; and have the [forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) traits.

 While in Mountain Stance, you gain a +4 item bonus to AC and a +2 circumstance bonus to any defenses against being [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or [Tripped](/Actions.aspx?ID=40). However, you have a Dexterity modifier cap to your AC of +0, meaning you don't add your Dexterity to your AC, and your Speeds are all reduced by 5 feet. The item bonus to AC from Mountain Stance is cumulative with [_armor potency runes_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=278) on your [explorer's clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=2), [_mage armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=176), and [_bracers of armor_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=416).

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 44

</column>

---

Dwarves have a long history fighting common foes, and you've mastered the ancient tactics to better face these enemies. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to damage with weapons and unarmed attacks against creatures with the [giant](/Traits.aspx?ID=79), [goblin](/Traits.aspx?ID=81), [hryngar](/Traits.aspx?ID=626), or [orc](/Traits.aspx?ID=124) trait. If your attack would deal more than one weapon die of damage (as is common at higher levels than 1st), the bonus is equal to the number of weapon dice or unarmed attack dice.

In addition, if any creature critically succeeds at an attack against you and deals damage to you, you gain your bonus to damage against that creature for 1 minute regardless of whether it has one of the listed traits

**Special** Your GM can add appropriate creature traits to the ancestral foes list if your character is from a community that commonly fights other types of enemies.

You instinctively create magical boats that keep your feet dry (mostly). You can walk on the surface of water and other non-damaging liquids, moving at half your normal Speed, as a magical boat forms under your feet to carry you. Your muse doesn’t fall into a single label. Choose a type of muse other than that of your own. You gain a 1st-level feat that requires that muse, and your muse is now also a muse of that type, allowing you to take feats with the other muse as a prerequisite. You don’t gain any of the other effects of the muse you chose.

**Special** You can take this feat multiple times. Each time you do, you must choose a different type of muse other than that of your own.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 52

**Archetype** [Mummy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=180)

**Prerequisites**
you are dead and were mummified (by natural or ritualistic means)

</column>

---

Whether through natural processes or foul rituals, your body was mummified, and you've risen as an undead mummy. You gain the [mummy](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=74) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) traits, as well as [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694).

 Many effects that harm the living are far less effective against your desiccated form. Unfortunately, your dried-out body is also highly flammable. You gain the [Toughness](/Feats.aspx?ID=855) feat, but also [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) weakness equal to half your level.

 Your fist draws moisture from the living by touch, making it more damaging and deadly. The damage die for your fist increases to 1d6 instead of 1d4, and your fist loses the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) trait.

 Finally, you become supernaturally bound to the dominant terrain in which you were created, either because you formed naturally from the weather of that terrain or because of the local ingredients and methods used in an intentional mummification process. Choose arctic, desert, mountain, or swamp. This choice can't be changed and may alter the effects of some of your feats.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the mummy archetype.

<title level="2">Mummy Dedication leads to...</title>
[Accursed Touch](/Feats.aspx?ID=3525), [Desiccating Inhalation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3530), [Ensnaring Wrappings](/Feats.aspx?ID=3528), [Grave Mummification](/Feats.aspx?ID=3523), [Mummy's Despair](/Feats.aspx?ID=3524), [One with the Land](/Feats.aspx?ID=3521), [Semblance of Life](/Feats.aspx?ID=3522), [Storm Shroud](/Feats.aspx?ID=3526), [Terrain Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=3529)

You force your mental anguish outward, projecting it upon those around you. You gain an aura of despair in a 30-foot emanation lasting 5 rounds. A creature that enters or begins its turn in the aura must succeed at a Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC or be [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) (frightened 2 on a critical failure). A creature that succeeds at the save is temporarily immune to Mummy's Despair for 10 minutes.

Bullets and bombs can be scarce in some parts, so you’ve learned to make your own. You become trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) and gain the advanced alchemy benefits. You can use the [advanced alchemy benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=3282) to create a number of daily consumables equal to 4 + half your level (rounded up); these consumables must be bombs or alchemical ammunition.

 You gain a [formula book](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2724) that includes the formula for black powder and four 1st-level types of common or uncommon alchemical ammunition or bombs of your choice.

 When crafting alchemical ammunition, including black powder in doses or rounds, using advanced alchemy, you create the ammunition in batches of 4 (meaning that if you were 4th level and used all of your advanced alchemy consumables to create alchemical ammunition, you could create a maximum of 24 rounds). You cannot use advanced alchemy to Craft horns or kegs of black powder.

Bullets and bombs can be scarce in some parts, so you’ve learned to make your own. You become trained in Crafting and gain the [alchemist’s infused reagents](/Classes.aspx?ID=56) class feature, gaining a number of reagents each day equal to your level. You also gain the [Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5117) feat and four additional formulas for 1st-level alchemical items. 

You gain infused reagents (a pool of reagents usable to make alchemical items) and advanced alchemy (allowing you to make alchemical items during your daily preparations without the normal cost or time expenditure). You gain batches of infused reagents per day equal to your level, which you can use to create only bombs or alchemical ammunition. Your advanced alchemy level for creating these is 1 and doesn’t increase on its own. If you use a batch of infused reagents to create basic level-0 ammunition such as [black powder](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1190) cartridges or black powder doses, you produce 10 rounds of ammunition.

Your familiar's supernatural spirit has outgrown its corporeal body. You can conduct a special 10-minute activity to reselect certain familiar abilities, switching one or more of the following abilities for other abilities on this list: [amphibious](/Familiars.aspx?ID=1), [burrower](/Familiars.aspx?ID=2), [climber](/Familiars.aspx?ID=3), [darkvision](/Familiars.aspx?ID=5), [fast movement](/Familiars.aspx?ID=6), [manual dexterity](/Familiars.aspx?ID=10), [resistance](/Familiars.aspx?ID=32), and [scent](/Familiars.aspx?ID=11). You can reselect only familiar abilities you would normally be able to reselect each day, not required familiar abilities for your familiar. You can't remove an ability that is required for another ability your familiar has (for instance, you can't remove manual dexterity if the familiar has [lab assistant](/Familiars.aspx?ID=9)).

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 68 --- Basic mutagens that affect your mind and thoughts can make you communicate telepathically, protect you from being detected, or let you communicate with anyone. While you're affected by one of the listed mutagens, you get an additional benefit.
  • **[Cognitive Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3316)** You also gain the mutagen's item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40), [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45), [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46), and [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks. In addition, you can communicate telepathically with creatures within 60 feet with whom you share a language. The communication is two-way once you establish it, so a creature you contact can also communicate with you.
  • **[Serene Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3320)** [Detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=574), [revelation](/Traits.aspx?ID=686), and [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) effects of 9th rank (or 17th level) or lower detect nothing from you or your possessions and auras. For instance, [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) would still detect other magic in the area, but not any magic on you.
  • **[Silvertongue Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3321)** Ignore circumstance penalties you would take to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks. In addition, your words transcend linguistic barriers; everyone listening to you speak hears your words as if you were speaking in their own language (though you don't actually speak that language, nor does this ability allow you to understand any additional languages).
**Special** If you can be under the effects of multiple mutagens (with the [mutagenist](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=7) greater field discovery, for example), you get all relevant benefits.

>
[My Kingdom, My Blood](/Feats.aspx?ID=7409) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 136

**Archetype** [Prophesied Monarch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=294)

**Prerequisites**
[Prophesied Monarch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7403)

</column>

---

The health of the ruler is the health of the kingdom, and the health of the kingdom is that of its ruler, each bound to the other inextricably. [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305). You can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type. You then plant your fist or weapon into the ground at your feet, creating a 60-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) in an aura around you that lasts for 1 minute. Whenever an ally within this aura takes damage, you can use your reaction to take half the damage in their stead while they take the remainder. When you take damage through this link, you don’t apply any [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893), weaknesses, or other abilities you have to that damage; you simply take that amount of damage. Whenever you take damage while this effect is active, an ally within the aura can use their reaction to take half the damage for you in the same manner.

The effect ends immediately if you’re reduced to 0 Hit Points.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

Long years of brave exploits haven’t gone unnoticed. Whether you know just the right things to say or those you’re speaking with recognize you as a reincarnated hero, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks made to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) or [Make An Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392), and to Intimidation checks made to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394). **Prerequisites**

---

Magic energy sustains you, supporting your form far beyond the capabilities of mere flesh. You can’t die except due to old age as long as you’re under the effects of an ongoing spell or within your _spellsurge_ aura; if your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) or [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) condition would increase to a high enough value to kill you, it doesn’t increase, and any effect that would instantly kill you instead just reduces you to 0 Hit Points.

If you die for any reason, you transform into a magical font attached to an allied creature of your choice within 1 mile. This creature gains knowledge of the [embodied font](/Rituals.aspx?ID=172) ritual to return you to your corporeal state. Until you’re restored, once per hour, you can cast _spellsurge_, centered on the chosen creature. You still make all choices for the _spellsurge_ and can take actions allowed by the spell, though you can take no other actions.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #216: The Acropolis Pyre](/Sources.aspx?ID=271) pg. 82

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Hero-God Lore ](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Trained in [Legendary Beast Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8)

**Trigger**
You successfully [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) to identify a creature that has the [mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835) trait.

</column>

---

Your ancestors confronted and bested mythic beasts of Iblydan antiquity. Through a combination of hearing these tales and channeling a hint of those warriors' mythic power, you've developed a knack for bypassing a mythic creature's fabled defenses. The next time you successfully Strike the triggering creature, your Strike treats its mythic resistance as 2 lower. You treat its resistance as 4 lower if your Hero-God Lore or Legendary Beast Lore proficiency rank is expert, 6 lower if your rank is master, and 8 lower if your rank is legendary.

 If your Strike would already ignore mythic resistance (because you are a mythic character or wield a mythic weapon), your next successful Strike against the creature instead deals an additional 1d6 precision damage. This additional damage increases to 1d8 if your Hero-God Lore or Legendary Beast Lore proficiency rank is expert, 1d10 if your rank is master, or 1d12 if your rank is legendary.

<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 65

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392); [hero-god accomplishment](/Rules.aspx?ID=3489)

</column>

---

Your myth includes amusing parables of clever plans and sly maneuvers, often applied to small things in life such as disguising yourself as a sheep to ambush a [wolf](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=485) or tricking a [snake](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=473) into shedding its skin. You can [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) as a two-action activity, regardless of how elaborate your tale. When you attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check, you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) to do so at [mythic proficiency](/Rules.aspx?ID=3322). If you succeed at a Deception check while in the presence of your hierophant, any of your worshippers that you can see automatically succeed at an attempt to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) or Lie in such a way that supports your story (for example, the target of your Lie claiming you are a teacher sees all of your worshippers as students). 

You also lay claim to one of the following domains of your choice: [confidence](/Domains.aspx?ID=67), [secrecy](/Domains.aspx?ID=91), or [trickery](/Domains.aspx?ID=94).

[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392); [hero-god accomplishment](/Rules.aspx?ID=3489)

</column>

---

Your myth speaks of distant travel to countless countries, planes, or dimensions. When any effect attempts to anchor you to a plane (such as [_planar tether_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1636)) or to banish you from the current plane (such as [_banishment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1448)), that effect gains the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait. If it already has the incapacitation trait, you gain a +4 status bonus to your save against the effect. If you successfully save against such an effect, the creature that attempted to use this effect on you must succeed at a Will save against your class or spell DC (whichever is higher) to avoid becoming [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 minute (stupefied 2 on a critical failure).

You also lay claim to one of the following domains of your choice: [dreams](/Domains.aspx?ID=72), [fate](/Domains.aspx?ID=75), or [travel](/Domains.aspx?ID=93).

You channel mythic power through your body and into a summoned ally, temporarily reinforcing them with a shared fraction of your mythic potential. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); the [summoned](/Traits.aspx?ID=706) creature gains a +2 status bonus to its attack rolls, a +2 status bonus to all of its defenses, and a number of additional Hit Points equal to your level that last for the duration of its summoning. The next [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) made by the summoned creature after you use this ability gains a +4 circumstance bonus to the attack roll.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />

**Prerequisites**
[Artisan's Calling](/MythicCallings.aspx?ID=2)

</column>

---

You infuse a receptacle, such as a normal bag, sack, or box, with mythic power, transforming it into a prison into which you can command a creature. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320), and attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check at mythic proficiency against the Will DC of a creature within 30 feet to trick, convince, or command it into entering the receptacle. The receptacle can hold a creature of any size, and the creature enters the receptacle if your check is successful. The creature is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1, and has to hold its breath or start [suffocating](/Rules.aspx?ID=2439). A creature trapped in the receptacle can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296); use the skill you used to lure the creature into the bag for the DC, and calculate the DC using mythic proficiency. The trapped creature is automatically freed after 1 minute, but you can spend an additional Mythic Point as a free action to prolong the duration of the containment for an additional minute when it would expire.

If the target of the counteract check is within your spellsurge aura, critical failures on this check are treated as failures.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 82

**Prerequisites**
[Quick Recognition](/Feats.aspx?ID=5197); ability to [cast spells](/Rules.aspx?ID=3144) from spell slots,; [Sage's Calling](/MythicCallings.aspx?ID=9)

**Trigger**
A creature Casts a Spell, you’ve successfully Recognized the Spell, and you have either a prepared spell or an unexpended spell slot of equal or greater rank.

</column>

---

You quench and counter your enemy’s magic with potent spellcraft amplified and enhanced by carefully deployed mythic power. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320), and expend a prepared spell or unexpended spell slot of the same rank as the triggering spell or higher. You lose your spell slot as if you’d cast the triggering spell. You then attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) the triggering spell using mythic proficiency to determine your spellcasting proficiency bonus for the counteract check.

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mythic Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7292) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 83

</column>

---

You convert your mythic power into a magical effect. When you gain this feat, choose up to three spells of 1st or 2nd rank that take no more than 3 actions to cast and that are either instantaneous or have a duration of 10 minutes or less. You can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to cast any of those spells for their normal action cost and use mythic proficiency to determine your [spell attack rolls](/Rules.aspx?ID=2292) and spell DCs, and the spells are automatically heightened to a rank equal to half your level (rounded up). If you don’t normally have the ability to cast spells, you use Charisma as your spellcasting attribute modifier; otherwise, you use the spellcasting ability associated with your spellcasting class. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity only for spells cast with this feat; you don’t otherwise gain the typical benefits of being a spellcaster.

**Special** At 14th level, add one spell of 3rd rank for you to cast using this ability. At 20th level, add one 4th-rank spell.

>
[Named Artillery](/Feats.aspx?ID=3223) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 128

**Archetype** [Artillerist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=115)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

It is a tradition among artillerists to name the [siege weapon](/SiegeWeapons.aspx) most important to them and closest to their heart—much as a sailor on a ship, the weapon is their livelihood. You've gone a step further, and you always make sure that your named artillery has the best possible maintenance and upkeep. You can spend a full day adjusting and working on a single siege weapon to designate it as your named artillery. The siege weapon you designated as your named artillery gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC, Fortitude saves, and Reflex saves as well as additional Hit Points equal to twice your level.

 During your daily preparations, you must spend at least one hour on maintenance to service your named artillery. If you fail to do so, or if you spend a full day designating a new piece of named artillery, the previous named artillery loses any benefits from this feat. Only one artillerist can designate a particular siege weapon as their named artillery, even if several artillerists are serving on the same siege weapon's crew (though it's typically more efficient for a group with several artillerists to divide them up, assigning one to each siege weapon).

fields.text: Feat 4 Named Artillery Archetype Skill Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 128 Archetype Artillerist Prerequisites Trained in Crafting It is a tradition among artillerists to name the siege weapon most important to them and closest to their heart—much as a sailor on a ship, the weapon is their livelihood. You've gone a step further, and you always make sure that your named artillery has the best possible maintenance and upkeep. You can spend a full day adjusting and working on a single siege weapon to designate it as your named artillery. The siege weapon you designated as your named artillery gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC, Fortitude saves, and Reflex saves as well as additional Hit Points equal to twice your level. <column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Nantambu Chime-Ringer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=106)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12); Trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14)

</column>

---

You've studied the basics of harmony and resonance in magic, exemplified by the ringing of chimes. You gain a single [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) or [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) cantrip of your choice, heightened to a spell level equal to half your level, rounded up. If you weren't already, you become trained in that tradition's spell DCs and spell attack rolls, with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability if you choose arcane or Charisma as your spellcasting ability if you choose occult. Regardless of your choice, you also either become trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or an expert in one of these skills if you are already trained in both.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Nantambu Chime-Ringer archetype.

<title level="2">Nantambu Chime-Ringer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Deny the Songs of War](/Feats.aspx?ID=3041), [Fleet Tempo](/Feats.aspx?ID=3040), [Sing to the Steel](/Feats.aspx?ID=3042), [Song of Grace and Speed](/Feats.aspx?ID=3043)

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=101" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Folklorist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=105)

**Prerequisites**
[Folklorist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3034)

</column>

---

You act as a conduit for your companions just as your stories are a conduit between teller and listener. When you Spin a Tale and the hero of your tale Casts a Spell against the villain, you warp the world, allowing the hero to calculate range and cover to the villain from your space instead of their own if they prefer. The hero must choose to calculate both range and cover from the same space; they can't use one space for range and the other for cover.

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 66 **Archetype** [Necrologist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=330) **Prerequisites** ability to cast spells from spell slots, ability to cast [_summon undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1706) --- Your studies of the lists of the dead allow you to call forth a horde of undead with a brief incantation. You can summon your horde with the Raise the Horde activity, and you can use the Mobbing Assault action while your horde is raised to command it to attack. The eerie connection you have with your horde precludes you from also having an animal companion or any other companion (such as a follower), though if an ability allows you to have more than one follower (such as with the [Additional Follower](/Feats.aspx?ID=7995) feat of the [captain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=332) archetype), you can count your horde as one. You have enough control over your horde that it doesn't attack you or your allies.
When raised, your horde is Huge and has a speed of 20 feet. It has the [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) traits. It can be attacked. Though it's made of several undead creatures, it can't share the same space as other creatures (unless you have certain feats). Due to your eldritch connection with your horde, it uses your AC, saves, and other defensive statistics like skill DCs, but is immune to the [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), and [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) conditions. The horde has [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) equal to your level to physical damage, but [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) equal to your level to area and splash damage. You share an animating force, so any damage that would be dealt to the horde is dealt to you instead, though you take damage only once from any ability that includes both you and the horde in the area of effect (though you take the greater amount of damage). **Raise the Horde** (concentrate, magical, manipulate) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** Your undead horde appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet. Choose whether your horde consists of skeletons or zombies, which affects the type of damage it deals with Mobbing Assault. Your horde remains summoned until the end of your next turn, but you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) the effect for up to 1 minute. The effect also ends if you end your turn more than 120 feet away from the horde. When you first use Raise the Horde and each time you Sustain the effect, you can have the horde Stride. When Raise the Horde ends, the undead that comprise your horde collapse lifelessly to the ground and quickly rot away. They can no longer be targeted or used for actions. **Mobbing Assault** (concentrate) **Requirements** Your horde has been raised; **Effect** Each enemy in a 5-foot emanation around your horde takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage (if your horde is zombies) or 2d6 slashing damage (if your horde is skeletons) with a basic Reflex save against your spell DC. At 10th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 2d6. Necrologist Dedication leads to... [Danse Macabre](/Feats.aspx?ID=7971), [Death Rattle](/Feats.aspx?ID=7974), [Deathguard](/Feats.aspx?ID=7968), [Dismal Harvest](/Feats.aspx?ID=7965), [Ghostsong](/Feats.aspx?ID=7969), [Grasping Corpses](/Feats.aspx?ID=7966), [Preserve the Horde](/Feats.aspx?ID=7970), [Shambling March](/Feats.aspx?ID=7967), [Shift Horde](/Feats.aspx?ID=7972)

You can cast spells like a necromancer, gaining a dirge with four common occult cantrips of your choice. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=4180) activity. You can prepare two cantrips each day from your dirge. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for necromancer archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are occult necromancer spells. You become trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44); if you were already trained in Occultism, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. 

Once per turn you can use a single action to create a single thrall within 30 feet. This action has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [necromancer](/Traits.aspx?ID=950), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), and [thrall](/Traits.aspx?ID=955) traits. You can use the Command a Thrall action as described in the thrall trait.

[Basic Death Dealing](/Feats.aspx?ID=9293), [Basic Necromancer Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=9294), [Inevitable Thralls](/Feats.aspx?ID=9297), [Necrotic Bomber](/Feats.aspx?ID=9295), [Thrall Charger](/Feats.aspx?ID=9296)

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 33 **Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175) (Level 12) **Prerequisites** ability to create or control [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160); [cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) with a negative font, [oracle](/Classes.aspx?ID=14) of [bones](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=3), or [necromancer](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=7) [wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=12) --- Necromantic energy demonstrates your power over undead, creating a demeanor that commands their fear and respect. Undead creatures can immediately sense your Necromancer's Visage and tend to act accordingly. If you take a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against an undead creature, it becomes permanently immune to your Necromancer's Visage, and your Necromancer's Visage ends. You can spend 10 minutes to restore your Necromancer's Visage, though any creatures that became permanently immune remain so. Each time an undead creature 2 or more levels lower than you attacks you, it must attempt a Will save against your spell DC. If you're also affected by [_sanctuary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=266) or a similar effect, only one affects the attacker (you choose which).
**Critical Success** The creature is permanently immune to your Necromancer's Visage.
**Success** The creature can attempt its attack and any other attacks against you this turn.
**Failure** The creature can't attack you and wastes the action. It can't attempt further attacks against you this turn.
**Critical Failure** The creature wastes the action and can't attempt to attack you as long as your Necromancer's Visage persists. **Special** This feat has the trait matching your spellcasting tradition.

You pour negative energy into your undead subject to empower its attacks. If the next action you use is to cast [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=146) to restore Hit Points to a single undead creature, the target then deals an additional 1d6 negative damage with its melee weapons and unarmed attacks until the end of its next turn. If the _harm_ spell is at least 5th level, this damage increases to 2d6, and if the _harm_ spell is at least 8th level, the damage increases to 3d6.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 166

**Archetype** [Celebrity](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=54)

**Prerequisites**
[Celebrity Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1931)

**Trigger**
You would gain the [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) condition.

**Requirements**
You are [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=27) by at least three creatures who aren't foes.

</column>

---

As long as you have an audience, you can continue to perform. Indeed, you must—you have an obligation to your fans! You delay the effects of the fatigued condition for 1 minute or until you are no longer observed by the required creatures, whichever comes first. If the fatigued condition has a duration, the duration begins to elapse only after the delay. You can't further delay or prevent the fatigued condition after this ability ends.

</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 49

---

The idea that you would hurt your companions, even when you've lost your reason, is unthinkable. Each time you would attack an ally due to being [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) or [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), you can attempt another saving throw against the effect that caused you to be confused or controlled with a +4 circumstance bonus to the save. If you succeed, you don't make the attack, though you still expend any actions it would have taken. If your save ends the effect making you confused or controlled, you can take any remaining actions during your turn as normal. Failing or critically failing this additional save doesn't increase the effect's duration or otherwise worsen it.

fields.text: Feat 16 Never! Guardian Source Battlecry! pg. 49 The idea that you would hurt your companions, even when you've lost your reason, is unthinkable. Each time you would attack an ally due to being confused or controlled, you can attempt another saving throw against the effect that caused you to be confused or controlled with a +4 circumstance bonus to the save. If you succeed, you don't make the attack, though you still expend any actions it would have taken. If your save ends the effect making you confused or controlled, you can take any remaining actions during your turn as normal. Failing or critically failing this additional save doesn't increase the effect's duration or otherwise worsen it.

A creature targets you with an attack and you can see the attacker.

---

Portents written in the night sky show you how to avoid an attack. The triggering attack roll targets your [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) DC instead of your AC. Though this allows you to avoid taking penalties to your AC, it doesn't remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with [sneak attack](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=34) would still deal extra damage to you for being [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16), even though you wouldn't take the –2 circumstance penalty when defending against the attack.

[Oatia Skysage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8112)

**Trigger**
A creature targets you with an attack and you can see the attacker.

**Requirements**
You can see the night sky.

</column>

---

Portents written in the night sky show you how to avoid an attack. The triggering attack roll targets your Occultism DC instead of your AC. Though this allows you to avoid taking penalties to your AC, it doesn’t remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with sneak attack would still deal extra damage to you for being [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), even though you wouldn’t take the –2 circumstance penalty when defending against the attack.

You can use [Retributive Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2807) at greater distance. You can use a ranged weapon to make a ranged Strike instead of a melee Strike for Retributive Strike. >
[Nimble Roll](/Feats.aspx?ID=4953) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 173

**Prerequisites**
[Nimble Dodge](/Feats.aspx?ID=4916)

</column>

---

You throw yourself into a roll to escape imminent danger. You can use Nimble Dodge before attempting a Reflex save in addition to its original trigger. If you do, the circumstance bonus applies to your Reflex save against the triggering effect.

When you use Nimble Dodge and the triggering attack fails or critically fails, or when you succeed or critically succeed at the saving throw, you can also Stride up to 10 feet as part of the reaction. If you do, the reaction gains the move trait. You can use Nimble Roll while Flying or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

When you use Nimble Dodge and the triggering attack fails or critically fails, or when you succeed or critically succeed at the saving throw, you can also Stride up to 10 feet as part of the reaction. If you do, the reaction gains the move trait. You can use Nimble Roll while Flying or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

<traits>

---

You are so used to wielding a shield that you can do so even while using the hand that's holding it for other purposes. The hand you use to wield a shield counts as a free hand for the purposes of the Interact action. You can also hold another object in this hand (but you still can't use it to wield a weapon). This benefit doesn't apply to [tower shields](/Shields.aspx?ID=4), which are still too cumbersome.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[No Hands, No Problems](/Feats.aspx?ID=6876) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Poppet" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=418" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 49

**Prerequisites**
[Tsukumogami Poppet](/Heritages.aspx?ID=383) heritage

</column>

---

After a lifetime of using temporary, ghostly limbs to manipulate objects, you hardly need real hands. You can extend your limbs to perform simple [Interact](/Rules.aspx?ID=2151) actions at a range 5 feet beyond your normal range, after which your limbs contract back to their normal length. You can also cast the [_telekinetic hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1715) cantrip as an arcane or occult innate spell at will, which always takes the ghostlike form of telekinetic hand and is tethered to your body via a snaking, illusory arm. A cantrip is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.

[No!!!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3683) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 28

**Trigger**
A non-[minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) ally within 60 feet is reduced to 0 Hit Points.

</column>

---

The shock of seeing your ally near death breaks whatever limits exist in your mind, sending your power spilling forth. If your psyche is currently unleashed, you can immediately use a [psyche](/Traits.aspx?ID=429) action that takes 1 action or less to use. If your psyche is not currently unleashed, you [Unleash your Psyche](/Actions.aspx?ID=1222), which remains unleashed until the end of your next turn. You can ignore Unleash Psyche's requirement of needing to have Cast a Spell on your previous turn, but you still can't Unleash your Psyche if you're [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) or for 2 rounds after your psyche subsides.

Certain plants and flowers hold a reputation throughout Tian Xia for being strong and upstanding, able to weather adversity. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[Noble Sacrifice](/Feats.aspx?ID=7410) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 136

**Archetype** [Prophesied Monarch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=294)

**Prerequisites**
[Prophesied Monarch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7403)

**Trigger**
One of your designated knights is within 15 feet of you and would take damage from an enemy’s [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

</column>

---

As your knights devote their lives and swords to you, so too do you return their devotion with your own fierce protection. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320). The knight [Steps](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) as a free action, and you [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) into the space previously occupied by the knight; this movement ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and greater difficult terrain. You then take the triggering damage instead. If you have a [shield raised](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316) and have the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction, you can use it as part of this ability, applying damage to the shield as though you were the original target of the attack. The enemy whose [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) triggered this reaction is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your next turn.

[Nocturnal Kindred](/Feats.aspx?ID=3548) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 58

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
[Vampire Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3545); Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)

</column>

---

You have an innate connection with other creatures of the night and understand some of them. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) with bats, rats, and wolves. You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on such animals.

 Once per day, you can cast [_animal allies_](/Spells.aspx?ID=863) as a divine innate spell, using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. The creatures it summons are bats, rats, and wolves. At 5th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the spell is heightened by an additional level, to a maximum of a 9th-level _animal allies_ when you are 19th level.

[Nodal Regeneration](/Feats.aspx?ID=5398) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Surki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=789" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 51

**Prerequisites**
[Nodal Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=5394)

</column>

---

Your body processes magic so effectively that you can induce true regeneration, replacing limbs and restoring organs. You can cast [_regenerate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1648) once per day as an innate spell. Instead of being deactivated by acid or fire, your regeneration from the spell is deactivated by [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), which slows your metabolism. You can target only yourself with the spell, but you can Cast the Spell as a reaction if you're reduced to 0 Hit Points by a non-cold effect.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 30

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

Many [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) wear masks when dealing with the living, and many cultures believe that seeing an unmasked psychopomp's face invites death. You are trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) and gain the [Intimidating Glare](/Feats.aspx?ID=796) skill feat. If you were already trained in Intimidation (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You also know how to make masks like those worn by psychopomps, a process that takes 1 hour and 1 sp of appropriate material. If you instead pay 50 gp for a splendid psychopomp mask, the mask grants you a +1 item bonus to Intimidation while you are wearing it. Its usage is worn (mask).

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 83 **Archetype** [Timewracked](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=340) **Prerequisites** [Timewracked Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8166) **Trigger** A creature targets you with a single-target spell or ability that you defend against with a saving throw or your AC. --- You reflexively attempt to cycle a creature’s timeline briefly to a reality where it’s less able to succeed. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323). The creature that targets you must then attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC at mythic proficiency, whichever is higher. **Critical Success** The spell or ability affects you normally.
**Success** The creature’s attempt to target you is slightly hindered. If your AC is being targeted, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC. If you need to attempt a saving throw, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the save.
**Failure** The creature’s attempt to target you is significantly hindered. If your AC is being targeted, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC, and a critical hit against you becomes a normal hit. If you need to attempt a saving throw, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the save, and if you critically fail, you fail instead.
**Critical Failure** The creature’s attempt to target you fails, and the actions it used to make the attempt are wasted.

>
[Nothing Personal](/Feats.aspx?ID=7694) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Blackjacket](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=316)

**Prerequisites**
[Mercenary Motivation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7691)

</column>

---

When you’re on a job, you can’t allow anyone to stop you. Designate a single creature you can see as being an impediment to your active course of action. The first time you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) your impediment in a round, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. At 14th level, this increases to two extra dice, and at 20th level, this increases to three extra dice. 

You can have only one creature designated as an impediment at a time. If you use Nothing Personal against a creature when you already have a creature designated, the prior creature loses the designation, and the new impediment gains the designation. Otherwise, your designation lasts for 1 hour.

    right="Feat 14"

[Nourishing Gate](/Feats.aspx?ID=4200) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 23

</column>

---

You can sustain yourself on a single drop of elemental dew or the slightest spark from the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6). You gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws against [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145), and effects that would make you [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28). You don't need to breathe, eat, or sleep, though you must still take a full night's rest every 24 hours to be able to make your daily preparations. During this time, you remain awake and alert, but you must spend the time meditating or attuning to your kinetic gate rather than engaging in other complex activities. Each kineticist attunes in their own individual way.

<title level="2">Nourishing Gate leads to...</title>
[Elemental Apotheosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=4203)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Nourishing Symbiosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=6682) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Yaksha" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=832" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 80

</column>

---

As you recuperate from your wounds, life energy flows from you to the land and back to you again. During downtime mode, when you take the [Long-Term Rest](/Rules.aspx?ID=2622) activity, you regain an additional 24 Hit Points after the first 24 hours of rest. You can use the [Subsist](/Rules.aspx?ID=2644) activity during a long-term rest and don’t need to spend any additional time to do so. When you do so, fruits, nuts, and vegetables sufficient to feed 5 people flourish overnight around you, ripe for the picking.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 81

**Archetype** [Timewracked](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=340)

**Prerequisites**
[Timewracked Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8166)

</column>

---

You flash through several possible timelines as you move. Stride up to your Speed. This movement doesn’t provoke reactions, and you are [concealed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2419) until the end of your turn. All creatures are [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to you until the end of your turn. You can use Now You See Me while [Burrowing](/Rules.aspx?ID=3373), [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Flying](/Rules.aspx?ID=3374), or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

---

You can mix alchemically preserved peppers into an alchemical food consumable to spice it up with alchemical fire. When the modified alchemical food is consumed, the user’s mouth goes numb temporarily. Once within the next hour, they can spend a single action to breathe a gout of flame in a 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386). Each creature in the cone takes 1d6 fire damage for every two levels you have with a basic Reflex save against your class DC.

[Oath of The Avenger](/Feats.aspx?ID=7517) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Oath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=119" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 276

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You’ve sworn an oath to punish wicked acts you witness. You gain the edict “hunt down those who have harmed innocents or committed heinous atrocities.” When you see a creature harm an ally, an innocent, or a noncombatant, you can invoke your oath against that creature. Like speaking, this doesn’t require an action. Most champions choose to invoke these oaths out loud if they’re able. The invocation lasts indefinitely, though you can choose to end if you are satisfied that the target has reformed, atoned, or been forgiven.

You can use [_lay on hands_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2047) to damage a creature you have invoked your oath against as if it were [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722); in this case, lay on hands deals [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage instead of [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) damage, gains the spirit trait, and loses the vitality trait. This doesn’t prevent you from healing such a creature with _lay on hands_ if you so choose.

[Oath of The Defender](/Feats.aspx?ID=7518) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Oath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=119" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 276

</column>

---

During your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), you can swear an oath to defend against a certain kind of enemy during your deeds that day. Choose [aberrations](/Traits.aspx?ID=523), [celestials](/Traits.aspx?ID=551), [dragons](/Traits.aspx?ID=581), [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), or [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722). You can’t choose celestials if you’re [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), nor can you choose fiends if you’re [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521). You gain an edict to defend against creatures of that kind.

Allies in your champion’s aura, not including you, get [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 2 to damage dealt by creatures with the chosen trait. If such a creature deals more than one damage type at once, apply this resistance only to the highest amount of damage. The resistance increases to 3 at 7th level, 4 at 12th level, and 5 at 17th level. If a creature with the chosen trait triggers your champion’s reaction and your champion’s reaction grants resistance against the triggering damage, the resistance increases by 5.

During your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), you can swear an oath to defeat, topple, or destroy a certain kind of enemy during your deeds that day. Choose [aberrations](/Traits.aspx?ID=523), [celestials](/Traits.aspx?ID=551), [dragons](/Traits.aspx?ID=581), [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), or [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722). Your [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) and devotion spells that deal damage do an additional 1 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage against a creature with the chosen trait. This damage increases to 2 at 7th level and 3 at 14th level. If a creature with the chosen trait triggers your champion’s reaction, this additional damage doubles until the end of your next turn.

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Your study of the stars unlocks supernatural insights and magic. You either become trained in [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or an expert in Occultism.

 You learn to cast spontaneous spells and gain the Cast a Spell activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common cantrips of your choice; these cantrips can be from any spell tradition, but they must be [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) spells. You cast these spells as occult spells as you draw on the stars and night sky. You're trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs. If you have a hand free and you've gazed at the night sky in the last 24 hours, you can usually replace material components with somatic components, so you don't need to use a spell component pouch. Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Oatia skysage archetype.

<title level="2">Oatia Skysage Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Skysage Divination](/Feats.aspx?ID=4065), [Minor Omen](/Feats.aspx?ID=4068), [Night's Glow](/Feats.aspx?ID=4067), [Night's Shine](/Feats.aspx?ID=4072), [Night's Warning](/Feats.aspx?ID=4073), [Scholar's Hunch](/Feats.aspx?ID=4069), [Stargazer's Eyes](/Feats.aspx?ID=4066), [Starlight Armor](/Feats.aspx?ID=4074), [Starlit Spells](/Feats.aspx?ID=4070)

You are, by nature, a thing of gloomy woods and barren wilds, and when you choose show yourself, a bit of this gloom clings to you, obscuring your form with strange distortions or mist. </title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Pathfinder Agent](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=13)

**Prerequisites**
[Pathfinder Agent Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=871)

</column>

---

Thanks to the time you've spent wandering through wild and untamed environments, you've gained an intuitive sense about creatures. You sometimes notice them before they attack, or spot them nearby even if they weren't planning on attacking. You can attempt a check to notice [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) creatures attempting to [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=511) nearby even if you aren't actively [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) for them. You still need to meet any other requirements to notice a particular creature.

---

Your blood contains a tiny fragment of unusual or inexplicable power from a mysterious dragon, such as a [conspirator dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=397) or [omen dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=403). You are drawn to the stranger parts of the world and can generally spot them with a glance. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44). If you would automatically become trained in Occultism (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the [Oddity Identification](/Feats.aspx?ID=5185) skill feat. If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose an occult dragon.

>
[Ocular Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=9147) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 39

</column>

---

You create a fleshy eyeball that is the size of a marble. You can take a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait, to look through any of your eyeballs until the start of your next turn. An eyeball can be manipulated like a marble, such as being rolled or thrown. One can also be affixed to a surface, for example a wall, with 1 minute’s work. An eyeball lasts for 24 hours, and you can maintain a total of three eyeballs at any given time. Creating a fourth destroys the oldest eyeball. 

Eyeballs are very small but are easy to spot. A creature actively [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) automatically finds an eyeball. They’re also not very sturdy and can be destroyed with an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action.

When you become aware of a magical effect or see a spell being cast, you can immediately determine if it twists minds (with the mental trait), fights against fortune (with the fortune or misfortune trait), or reveals secrets (with the detection, prediction, revelation, or scrying traits).     level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[On Borrowed Time](/Feats.aspx?ID=8527) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursebound" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=800" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=817" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 189

**Prerequisites**
[time mystery](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=23)

</column>

---

You accelerate a foe's personal timestream, which causes them to experience time at a faster rate, putting a terrible strain on their mind and body. A creature you target within 30 feet takes 3d6 [persistent mental damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) with a basic Will save. At the end of the subject's turn, they take this persistent damage after all other persistent damage. Before they roll their flat check to end the persistent damage, an additional round passes for them; this affects the duration of all beneficial effects, negative effects, afflictions, conditions, and other persistent damage. The subject attempts saving throws, flat checks, and any other rolls and takes damage as if the time had passed. They don't take the persistent mental damage from On Borrowed Time more than once per round.

 If you are cursebound 2 when you use On Borrowed Time, the persistent damage increases to 4d6. If you are cursebound 3 when you use On Borrowed Time, the persistent damage increases to 5d6.

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 79 **Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339) **Frequency** once per hour **Prerequisites** [Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151) --- Be they in your current life or your previous one, you’ve had many heroic moments that continue to inspire you. Even past failures or humiliations can become a source of inspiration—or at least, an opportunity to make up for a past error on this new day. Attempt an Incarnation Lore check against a very hard DC of your level. **Critical Success** You gain a +3 status bonus to AC and [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to physical damage equal to your level until the end of your next turn. You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this effect for up to 1 minute.
**Success** As critical success, but the status bonus is +2 and the resistance is equal to half your level.
**Failure** You gain a +1 status bonus to AC until the end of your next turn.
**Critical Failure** You gain a +1 status bonus to AC against the next attack made against you until the end of your next turn.

>
[Once and Future](/Feats.aspx?ID=7417) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 137

**Archetype** [Prophesied Monarch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=294)

**Prerequisites**
[Prophesied Monarch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7403)

</column>

---

Though foul treachery might lay you low or dark magic still your heart, when the people cry out for you in desperate need, you shall rise to protect them. You can’t die except due to old age as long as one of your knights is alive and within 30 feet; if your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) or [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) condition would increase to a high enough value to kill you, it doesn’t increase, and any effect that would instantly kill you instead just reduces you to 0 Hit Points. The first time each year you would die for any reason other than old age, you instead return to life and consciousness with a number of Hit Points equal to twice your level and gain a Mythic Point. If you ever truly die and aren’t returned to life within 1 year, you’re reborn as a child into a new mortal body somewhere in the world where stories of your accomplishments are still told. You don’t complete your journey along the River of Souls until all mortal memory of you has vanished.

[One Among The Masses](/Feats.aspx?ID=7308) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 107

**Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287)

**Prerequisites**
[Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304)

</column>

---

It will take more than a gathered mass of foes to take you down. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) equal to your level to damage dealt by [swarms](/Traits.aspx?ID=707), [troops](/Traits.aspx?ID=367), and creatures who occupy the same space as you. In addition, you can briefly menace large groups of enemies to step aside. You gain the Overawe Crowd activity.

**Overawe Crowd** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Requirements** You are sharing the same space as a [swarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=707) or are adjacent to a [troop](/Traits.aspx?ID=367); **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point and attempt an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check at mythic proficiency against the Will DC of the required swarm or troop. On a failure, the target Strides in a direction of your choosing and you move along with it. On a success, the target Strides twice in a direction of your choosing and you can decide whether or not to move along with it. No matter the result, the target is stunned 1 and temporarily immune to your Overawe Crowd for 24 hours.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[One Life, Two Vessels](/Feats.aspx?ID=7356) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

</column>

---

The minds of you and your [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) are so intertwined that, so long as one of you lives, the other continues to exist in the living one’s mind. If your united companion ever dies or is [destroyed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=46) and it is within 30 feet of you, its consciousness is drawn into your mind, where it can communicate with you normally and remains there until your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575). During your next daily preparations, you can call upon your union to restore your companion to life again in a ritual that takes 1 hour. Your restored united companion returns whole-bodied, at their maximum Hit Point total, and cured of any afflictions that may have been afflicting it when it died.

If you would ever die or be destroyed and you are within 30 feet of your united companion, you consciousness flows into your companion for 3 days. During this time, you can perform actions as if you are your united companion using its abilities and characteristics for any actions you perform. After spending 3 days in this state, you are returned to life with a number of Hit Points equal to twice your level and regain a Mythic Point.

If you or your united companion die while sharing your body with the other’s consciousness, you truly die, but if you are not returned to life within 1 year, you are both reincarnated as children (or in a similarly immature state) in a location near where you first became companions. Neither you nor your companion complete your journeys along the River of Souls, nor do you possess any knowledge of the other’s reincarnated form. However, you both feel an inkling of your former connection, should you ever meet. If either of you are killed before you are together again as companions, the cycle of reincarnation is broken, and you can both die as normal.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[One with the Spirits](/Feats.aspx?ID=7587) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 294

**Archetype** [Rivethun Invoker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=309)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Rivethun Invoker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7581)

**Requirements**
You’re under the effects of Enter Spirit Trance.

</column>

---

The spirits you’ve invoked throughout your life have left behind echoes and spiritual fragments, which you can manifest across your own flesh, temporarily transforming you into something more akin to spirit than mortal. For 1 minute, you gain [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 5 and you become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62). You can’t use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404). Your [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) gain the benefits of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) property rune. Whenever you deal damage with a Strike, you can choose to have that Strike deal [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, rather than its usual damage type.

If you would be knocked [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) value would increase while One with the Spirits is active, the spirits revive you at the beginning of your next turn, restoring you to 30 Hit Points. One with the Spirits then immediately ends.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 129

**Prerequisites**
expert strikes

</column>

---

You put all your force into a single mighty, carefully controlled blow. Make an unarmed Strike. If you spend two actions and this Strike hits, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. You can instead spend 3 actions to perform an even more powerful attack, dealing a second additional die of weapon damage on a hit.

 If you're at least 10th level, the number of additional dice you add from this feat doubles, for a total of 2 additional dice if you spend 2 actions or 4 additional dice if you spend 3 actions. If you're at least 18th level, the number of additional dice you add from this feat triples, for a total of 3 additional dice if you spend 2 actions or 6 additional dice if you spend 3 actions.

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Oni Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6835) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Hungerseed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=827" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 36

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

</column>

---

Your horns flash briefly as you grow in size and ferocity. Your size increases to Large, and you’re [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1. This doesn’t change your Speed, reach, or other statistics except as noted here. Your worn equipment automatically resizes to suit your new form, though it immediately returns to its original size if it leaves your possession. This form is the same age and body type as your true form and has roughly analogous physical traits, such as hair color. Using Oni Form counts as creating a disguise for the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) use of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38). You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) your Oni Form for up to 10 minutes, though you must then spend at least 10 minutes in your natural form before using Oni Form again.

<title level="2">Oni Form leads to...</title>
[Greater Transformation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7118)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Hungerseed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=827" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 36

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The Oni Weapon Familiarity feat also grants access to the listed weapons._

</column>

---

Oni prefer large, cruel weapons for smashing their foes to pieces, and so do you. For the purposes of proficiency, you treat the [khakkhara](/Weapons.aspx?ID=412), [nodachi](/Weapons.aspx?ID=298), ogre hook, and [tetsubo](/Weapons.aspx?ID=493) as simple weapons.

The [ogre hook](/Weapons.aspx?ID=495) is an uncommon martial weapon that costs 1 gp, deals 1d10 piercing damage, has 2 Bulk, requires two hands to use, is in the pick weapon group, and has the deadly d10 and trip weapon traits.

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, or with your horns unarmed Strike, you get its critical specialization effect.

<traits>

<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 36

</column>

---

You can designate your ikons as movable by only your own hand, leaving them fixed in place as surely as if they were lodged in stone. Whenever you Release an ikon, you can spend an action to command it to remain motionless. While motionless, the ikon can be moved only if 8,000 pounds of pressure are applied to it or if a creature uses [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) to Force Open the ikon with a DC equal to your class DC. You can Release your ikon over an adjacent prone enemy to hold them down with the ikon’s motionlessness—while so Released, you can’t use the ikon, but the enemy must succeed at the Athletics check to Stand or to move. The ikon automatically flies back to your hand when the effect is broken or if you spend an Interact action to hold out a hand and draw it back.

fields.text: Feat 4 Only the Worthy Exemplar Ikon Source War of Immortals pg. 36 You can designate your ikons as movable by only your own hand, leaving them fixed in place as surely as if they were lodged in stone. Whenever you Release an ikon, you can spend an action to command it to remain motionless. While motionless, the ikon can be moved only if 8,000 pounds of pressure are applied to it or if a creature uses Athletics to Force Open the ikon with a DC equal to your class DC. You can Release your ikon over an adjacent prone enemy to hold them down with the ikon’s motionlessness—while so Released, you can’t use the ikon, but the enemy must succeed at the Athletics check to Stand or to move. The ikon automatically flies back to your hand when the effect is broken or if you spend an Interact action to hold out a hand and draw it back.
