    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Oozemorph Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2185) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from The Slithering</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Slithering](/Sources.aspx?ID=41) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Oozemorph](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=84)

</column>

---

You are plagued by sporadic anatomical rearrangements, which grant you insights into other creatures with unusual anatomies. You become trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) and [Ooze Lore](/Traits.aspx?ID=122); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Reflex saves to avoid being [Engulfed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=14) by creatures, and to checks to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) after being Engulfed.

 As you develop more abilities based on your amorphous affliction, you become increasingly off-putting to mundane creatures. You take a penalty to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks against [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) and [humanoids](/Traits.aspx?ID=91). This penalty is equal to your number of class feats from the oozemorph archetype, to a maximum of –4 for four or more feats.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the oozemorph archetype.

<title level="2">Oozemorph Dedication leads to...</title>
[Disturbing Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=2186), [Hideous Ululation](/Feats.aspx?ID=2187), [Ooze Empathy](/Feats.aspx?ID=2189), [Uncanny Suction](/Feats.aspx?ID=2191), [Vacate Vision](/Feats.aspx?ID=2188)

---

Thanks to your diligence in the study of divine and occult mysteries, you can focus to temporarily attain a perception beyond the ordinary. A lightless flame appears in the center of your forehead. For 1 minute, you gain the benefits of a [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) spell. In addition, when you attempt a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) during this time against a creature about which you could [Recall Knowledge](/Rules.aspx?ID=2638) using [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46), the attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) required due to the target being [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79).

</column>

---

Choose a [mystery](/Mysteries.aspx). You become trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) and the mystery's skill; if you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the mild, constant effects of the mystery's curse described in its first paragraph, but not other effects the mystery usually grants. You cast spells like an oracle and gain the Cast a Spell activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two cantrips, either common divine cantrips or other divine cantrips you learn or discover. You're trained in divine spell attack rolls and divine spell DCs. Your key spellcasting ability for oracle archetype spells is Charisma, and they are divine oracle spells.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the oracle archetype.

<title level="2">Oracle Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Mysteries](/Feats.aspx?ID=1852), [Basic Oracle Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=1853), [First Revelation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1854)

>
[Oracular Warning](/Feats.aspx?ID=1497) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 80

**Trigger**
You are about to roll initiative.

</column>

---

You have a flash of insight about impending danger related to one ally, and you can shout or gesture to warn that ally of the threat a moment before it materializes. One ally of your choice can roll twice for initiative and use the better result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. If you are legendary in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13), you receive two visions and can warn two allies, granting them both this benefit.

 You are momentarily thrown off by the divine insight, however, and you must roll twice for your initiative roll and use the worse result. This is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect. The two effects are tied together; if you would avoid the misfortune effect for any reason, or if any of your allies would negate their fortune effect, your Oracular Warning does nothing. Depending on whether you use gestures or call out, this action gains either the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) or [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait, respectively.

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 58 **Archetype** [Field Propagandist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=326) **Prerequisites** [Field Propagandist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7922) --- When you seek to convince others of the worth of your cause, you are capable of unleashing such an entrancing torrent of rhetoric and metaphor that it is all but impossible to look away from you. When you begin a conversation or similar attempt with the goal of [Making an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392), all creatures who are observing you become [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) unless they succeed at a Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. Creatures who are familiar with you and your verbal techniques, such as allies you've known for at least several days, are immune to this effect, though newer allies who have not heard one of your speeches before might still be affected.

Affected creatures remain fascinated for as long as you continue your filibuster, though they can attempt a new save to end the effect at the end of each minute while your filibuster lasts. A creature who succeeds at a saving throw to end the fascinated condition from your filibuster is also unaffected by your attempt to Make an Impression.

You can continue your filibuster indefinitely, but after every 10 minutes you must attempt a Fortitude saving throw against a hard DC for your level. Failing this save results in your filibuster ending and prevents you from attempting another filibuster for 1 hour.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Orbiting Runestone](/Feats.aspx?ID=9205) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 52

</column>

---

You create a runestone that floats around you, and you [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) with a damaging invocation on it even if the rune could not normally be applied to an object. The runestone has 10 Hit Points. Each time a creature successfully [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) you, attempt a DC 11 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). On a success, the runestone blocks the attack, so the attack first damages the runestone and then applies any remaining damage to you. If this damage reduces the runestone to 0 Hit Points, it explodes outward toward the attacker. If the attacker is within 15 feet, the rune etched upon the runestone invokes automatically, applying its invocation effect to the attacker. The attacker is the only one affected by the invocation, even if the rune could normally affect multiple creatures.

The runestone’s magic is capable of maintaining the traced rune for up to 1 minute as it floats around you, at which point the rune fades and the runestone shatters. You can maintain only a single orbiting rune at any given time. If you try to create a second, the first one shatters.

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 50 --- You paint your face to create a _warmask_, an invested magic item of negligible Bulk with an item level equal to your level and a usage of worn (mask). It has the [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) trait and a magical tradition trait depending on its type. Donning or removing your _warmask_ requires 1 minute of work, though you don't need to Invest the mask each time. The _warmask_ is unique to you and might signify your hold, your accomplishments, or your faith. While creating your mask, you must choose the source of your _warmask's_ power from the options below. This source determines the mask's associated skill as well as magical tradition. Once you select this source, it can't be changed. You become trained in the associated skill, and you gain the [Dubious Knowledge](/Feats.aspx?ID=776) skill feat as a bonus feat. You can spend 1 hour performing a ceremony that costs 50 gp to attune yourself more deeply with your _warmask_. If you do, you gain a +1 item bonus to the associated skill whenever you wear the _warmask_.
  • **The Gods** [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) tradition
  • **The Land** [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134) tradition
  • **Magic** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11) tradition
  • **The Unknown** [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) tradition
Orc Warmask leads to... [Mask of Fear](/Feats.aspx?ID=2423), [Mask of Pain](/Feats.aspx?ID=2421), [Mask of Power](/Feats.aspx?ID=2417), [Mask of Rejection](/Feats.aspx?ID=2418)

You have learned the secrets of another druidic order, passing whatever rites of initiation that order requires and gaining access to its secrets. Choose an order other than your own. You gain a 1st-level feat that lists that order as a prerequisite, and you are now a member of that order for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites. If you commit acts anathema to your new order, you lose all feats and abilities requiring that order but retain your other druid feats and abilities. You don’t gain any of the other benefits of the order you chose.

**Special** You can take this feat multiple times. Each time you do, you must choose a different order other than your own.

If the next action you take is to [Manifest your Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757) as a three-action activity, or to Cast a three-action summoning Spell, the creature appears in an explosion.     level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Osteo Armaments](/Feats.aspx?ID=9110) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 35

</column>

---

If you have bones, you have a weapon. You create a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) weapon_ in which you are proficient, made of bone and sinew. If this weapon requires [ammunition](/Rules.aspx?ID=3193), mundane bone ammunition is created when you [reload](/Rules.aspx?ID=2196) it. The weapon falls apart and is destroyed after 1 hour, if you aren’t holding the weapon at the end of your turn, or if you use this action again, whichever comes first. 

At 8th level, you can destroy an adjacent thrall as part of using this action. If you do, the action gains the [thrall](/Traits.aspx?ID=955) trait and the weapon also gains a [_decaying_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2835) rune, or the _greater decaying_ rune if you’re 15th level or higher.

At 10th level, the weapon improves to a _+2 striking weapon_, increasing to a _+2 greater striking weapon_ at 12th level, a _+3 greater striking weapon_ at 16th level, or a _+3 major striking weapon_ at 19th level.

    right="Feat 2"

>
[Ostilli Host Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5451) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 70

**Archetype** [Ostilli Host](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=222)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

**Access**
surki ancestry

</column>

---

You've bonded with an attached symbiote known as an ostilli. You can bond with only one ostilli at a time since the symbiote emits low-frequency magical pulses that repel other ostillis. You become trained in [Ostilli Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41); if you were already trained, you become an expert.

 The ostilli is a Tiny creature [grafted](/Rules.aspx?ID=3275) to your body. Like other grafts, it has no Hit Points or Speeds of its own and can't be targeted separately. It can't be removed and dies when you do; in the event of your demise and resurrection, you can bond to a new ostilli during a week of downtime, though you lose any abilities granted by your ostilli bond during that time. Your ostilli is obvious, unless you attempt to cover it with clothing or armor. In such a case, an onlooker can determine you're bonded to an ostilli with a successful [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Perception, or Surki Lore check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) DC. Your ostilli must be visible for you to use any of the actions it grants.

 Your ostilli is constantly siphoning ambient magic from the surroundings, granting you the Repel Ambient Magic and Spit Ambient Magic actions.

 **Repel Ambient Magic** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) Your ostilli glows green as it absorbs magic. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against the next [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) attack, cantrip, or spell that targets you. This bonus increases to +2 at 12th level.

 **Spit Ambient Magic** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** Your ostilli flashes red as it regurgitates a dart of magic at a target within 30 feet. This magical dart deals 1d6 piercing damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC). This damage increases by 1d6 at 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter.

<title level="2">Ostilli Host Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cellular Reconstruction](/Feats.aspx?ID=5462), [Chaining Mutation](/Feats.aspx?ID=5458), [Cloaking Pulse](/Feats.aspx?ID=5455), [Deadly Mutation](/Feats.aspx?ID=5459), [Deflecting Pulse](/Feats.aspx?ID=5456), [Propulsive Mutation](/Feats.aspx?ID=5457), [Soothing Pulse](/Feats.aspx?ID=5452), [Spell Swallow](/Feats.aspx?ID=5460), [Spraying Mutation](/Feats.aspx?ID=5461), [Tactile Magic Feedback](/Feats.aspx?ID=5453), [Versatile Mutation](/Feats.aspx?ID=5454)

The arcane magic you possess grows in power and complexity. Choose one common 2nd-level spell from the same tradition as an innate spell you previously gained from another elf ancestry feat (from the arcane list if you have [Otherworldly Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=17), for example). <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ouroboric Pact](/Feats.aspx?ID=7448) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 46

**Archetype** [Pactbinder](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=189)

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbinder Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3822); Master in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)

</column>

---

You’ve studied pacts at Cobyslarni, or learned under someone who has, and understand them to not only create a bargain between individuals, but a separate entity altogether: the pact itself. You gain the Entreat Pact action, which you can use in association with any pact from the pactbinder archetype. For example, if you have the Pact of Draconic Fury, you could Entreat Pact to aid a skill check to obtain an item the dragon desires. 

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> Entreat Pact;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You attempt a skill check directly related to the conditions of the pact;  **Effect** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) You call upon the occult energies powering your pact to help you fulfill your promise. Roll twice on the triggering check and take the better result.

**Special** Your pacts continually enforce themselves in a circular magical loop. You lose the ability to retrain out of any feats from the pactbinder archetype.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Out of Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3563) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 61

**Archetype** [Zombie](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=182)

**Prerequisites**
[Zombie Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3557)

</column>

---

Even when your limbs are severed, they remain a part of you. When an arm is severed from your body, it gains the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) trait. While severed, your limb has the statistics of a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=160) without any familiar or master abilities, except its Speed is 5 feet, it can't move further than 100 feet from you, it can Interact with things, and it can still make any [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strikes it could have made while attached to you (usually a fist Strike). Any Strikes it makes share your multiple attack penalty and use your attack bonus and damage. If your arm is reduced to 0 HP or is ever more than 100 feet from you, it becomes inert until reattached. The GM might allow you to detach other limbs that have unarmed attacks using the below action (for example, if you're a tiefling with [Form of the Fiend](/Feats.aspx?ID=1379), giving you a tail unarmed attack).

 You gain the Lay Down Arms action.

 **Lay Down Arms** <actions string="Single Action" /> You pull your arm off, harmlessly severing it from your body and dropping it in an adjacent square. You can also use this action to reattach your severed arm if it's adjacent to you; it immediately functions normally. If the detached limb was at 0 Hit Points, it takes 10 minutes to reattach it instead of a single action.

You have learned how to weigh down your enemies’ life essence.     right="Feat 10"

>
[Overloaded Ammunition](/Feats.aspx?ID=9199) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 51

</column>

---

You can tenuously bind power into arrows or sling stones to transform them into explosive missiles. During your daily preparations, you can lay power-containing runes upon two pieces of mundane ammunition to transform them into [_explosive ammunition_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2923). The DC of the explosive ammunition is equal to your class DC. The binding on the powder is unstable, and the ammunition burns itself to ash by your next daily preparations if not used. This ammunition has no value if sold.

At 14th level, you create _greater explosive ammunition_ instead.

>
[Oversized Throw](/Feats.aspx?ID=1606) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=135" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 109

**Requirements**
You have one or more hands free.

</column>

---

With a great heave, you seize a piece of your surroundings, such as a boulder, log, table, wagon, or chunk of earth, and hurl it at your foes. The object must be your size or one size smaller than you, and it must not have too much Bulk for you to lift it in the first place. Make a ranged Strike with the object; regardless of the result, the object takes the same amount of damage it would deal on a success. The object is a simple ranged weapon that deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage, has a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 20 feet, and has the [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapon trait. The damage increases to 2d10 if you have weapon specialization in simple weapons, or 3d10 if you have greater weapon specialization.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Overwatch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3118) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 50

**Archetype** [Overwatch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=109)

**Prerequisites**
expert in Perception

</column>

---

You have an innate knack for tactical observation, and you’ve innovated to apply that knack in a variety of ways that allow you to assist your allies. With the help of enhanced visual gear (such as a specially modified telescope, goggled visor, or binoculars) and a set of carefully curated signals to share the information you uncover with your allies, you and your team are always keenly aware of the movement of combatants on the battlefield. You quickly and efficiently disperse the information you discover to your nearby allies so they can use it to direct their own observations and reactions to danger.

You’re surrounded by an overwatch field aura in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Your overwatch field aura grants you increased perception and allows you to call out warnings to your allies within the aura to point out threats. This aura has the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) and [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) traits. When you roll [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2882) for initiative, you and allies within your overwatch field receive a +2 circumstance bonus on your initiative rolls.

<title level="2">Overwatch Dedication leads to...</title>
[Control Tower](/Feats.aspx?ID=3125), [Converge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3126), [Forewarn](/Feats.aspx?ID=3123), [Master Spotter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3124), [Spyglass Modification](/Feats.aspx?ID=3119), [Swift Intervention](/Feats.aspx?ID=3120), [Topple Giants](/Feats.aspx?ID=3121), [Wide Overwatch](/Feats.aspx?ID=3122)

You throw your weight into a powerful attack that leaves you vulnerable. Make a melee Strike. This counts as three attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. You control your breathing and align it with your ki, exhaling with controlled force in order to overcome your opponent's resistance. If you use your next action to Cast a Spell that has the [monk](/Traits.aspx?ID=112) trait and no duration, the spell and any Strikes you make as a result of casting it ignore an amount of the target's resistance to physical damage equal to your level.

    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Overwhelming Energy](/Feats.aspx?ID=337) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=52" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 200

</column>

---

You alter your spells to overcome resistances. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, the spell ignores an amount of the target’s resistance to acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage equal to your level. This applies to all damage the spell deals, including persistent damage and damage caused by an ongoing effect of the spell, such as the wall created by [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362). A creature’s immunities are unaffected.

You and your companion move to take down a common enemy. You and your animal companion both Stride. If both of you end your movement within reach of the same creature, you and your animal companion each make a melee Strike against the creature. You can use Pack Movement to [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Stride if both you and your animal companion have the corresponding movement type.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You and your united [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) call upon the service of others of its kind, creating figment duplicates of your companion to form a massive swarm of formidable power. Spend a Mythic Point. Your united companion becomes Gargantuan for 1 minute. It gains [immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2313) to precision damage, [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to physical damage equal to half your level, and a [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) to area damage equal to half your level. While in this form, your united companion gains the Amassed Assault action, which you immediately Command them to use as the final step of this activation. 

**Amassed Assault** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540)) Each enemy in your united companion's space takes damage equal to one of its unarmed Strikes plus your level ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 166

**Archetype** [Pactbinder](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=189)

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbinder Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3822)

</column>

---

You've sworn a pact with a [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50), giving you the ability to tap into the dragon's immeasurable power in exchange for adding to their hoard. You gain the Dragon Breath activity. In exchange, you promise to search for objects the dragon wants for its hoard upon request. These requests might be extremely specific unique objects, or they might be a broad category of objects. While the dragon agrees to pay you a fair price for the item you retrieve, the pact requires you to give your time and service.

 **Dragon Breath** <actions string="Two Actions" /> **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You breathe deeply and exhale a line or cone of powerful breath, much like the dragon with which you made the pact. If the dragon had a cone-shaped breath weapon, your breath weapon is a 30-foot cone. If they had a line-shaped breath weapon, your breath weapon is a 60-foot line. If they had a burst-shaped breath weapon, your breath weapon is a 10-foot burst within 60 feet. No matter the shape, it deals 1d6 damage per level, of the same damage type as the dragon's Breath Weapon, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save, using the higher of your class DC or spell DC. This action has the same traits as the breath weapon of the dragon you made the pact with.

[Pact of Eldritch Eyes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3828) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 167

**Archetype** [Pactbinder](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=189)

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbinder Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3822)

</column>

---

You've sworn a pact with an entity beyond mortal comprehension, granting you distant visions and insights. You can cast [_prying eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=239) as an occult innate spell once per hour, using the higher of your class DC and your spell DC to determine the DC.

 In exchange, you allow the entity to peer through you at your world. The entity's touch creates strange dreams, typically nightmares. Every morning, you awaken trained in an unexpected [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill determined by the GM, which you retain until the next time you rest for the night. While the entity contacts you most often while you sleep, it occasionally peers at you during the day, leading to disorientation and visions. You can generally determine what's going on during these visions, so normally this occurrence imparts no mechanical penalty. </column>

---

You've sworn a pact with [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) powers, granting you the otherworldly appearance of your dreams in exchange for oaths of hospitality. As long as you keep your end of the bargain, your base appearance changes indefinitely to any one appearance you wish that's within the bounds of possibility for your ancestry; this effect can't be [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) or removed except by violating the pact. Additionally, you can cast [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159) as a primal innate spell once per hour, using the higher of your class DC and your spell DC to determine the DC.

 In exchange, you promise to accept any fey's request for hospitality, granting them food, drink, and lodging for up to 3 days and 3 nights. You also promise not to harm any creature to whom you've offered hospitality or who has shown hospitality to you, whether or not that creature is fey, unless that creature does harm first. If you refuse hospitality to a fey or violate hospitality, you lose the benefits of this feat until you atone for your transgressions, instantly reverting your appearance to the one you had before the pact.

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbinder Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3822)

</column>

---

You’ve sworn a pact with Zemnaïdé, a huldra professor at Cobyslarni, to help renew his former homeland of the Sarkoris Scar. You can cast [_entangling flora_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1515) as a primal innate spell once per day. After the spell ends, the flowers and vines become mundane plants that can continue surviving if the natural environment can support them. They’re no longer difficult terrain, and don’t have the other effects of the spell. Fiends that fail a save against this spell or another plant spell you cast become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 in addition to the normal effects.

 In exchange for her boon, Zemnaïdé requires that you never knowingly aid demons or their allies, nor despoil a natural environment. If you do either, you lose the benefits of this feat until you atone. If you comment on his bovine tail or imply the huldras are connected to trolls, Zemnaïdé revokes the benefits of this feat for 1 week or until you sincerely apologize.

---

You've sworn a pact with [devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30), granting you success in life in exchange for your soul in the afterlife. Once per hour, when you critically fail a check, you can reroll the check as a free action; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. Additionally, you can choose to automatically succeed at checks to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23) for tasks below your level, without rolling.

 However, when you die, your soul is consigned to [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=18). You can't be returned to life except by powerful magic such as [_miracle_](/Spells.aspx?ID=196), and even then, the devils responsible for the contract can track your every move for 1 year. The devils gain the effects of a [_discern location_](/Spells.aspx?ID=75) spell. They can also use 10th-level [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268) on you at will, and you automatically critically fail your saving throw.

**Special** You can't retrain out of a Pact of Infernal Prowess without journeying to Hell and destroying the devil's written contract spelling out the terms of your pact.

You’ve sworn a pact with Ng the Hooded, the Eldest known as the Lord of the Crossroads, though your only sign of Ng’s acknowledgment is the benefits you receive. Anyone tracking you must succeed at a Survival check against the higher of your class DC and spell DC. Creatures attempting to remember your features after the first time meeting you must succeed at a Will save against the same DC. If they fail, they recall the meeting but none of your features.

 In exchange, you must continue your wanderings, never settling in one place for longer than one month, or you lose the benefits of this feat until you begin your travels again. If you ever willingly tell anyone you’ve formed a pact with Ng, you lose the benefits of this feat permanently, though you can share vague information about the pact’s effects.

Creatures attempting to remember your features after the first time meeting you must succeed at a Will save against the same DC. If they fail, they recall the meeting but none of your features. In exchange, you must continue your wanderings, never settling in one place for longer than one month, or you lose the benefits of this feat until you begin your travels again. If you ever willingly tell anyone you’ve formed a pact with Ng, you lose the benefits of this feat permanently, though you can share vague information about the pact’s effects.

You’ve sworn a pact with a psychopomp bent on the destruction of all undeath. You gain an imprecise deathsense that can detect undead creatures up to 60 feet away. Additionally, whenever an undead creature is destroyed within 60 feet you gain temporary Hit Points equal to its level that last for 1 minute.

 In exchange, the psychopomp requires that you never aid in the creation or conquest of an undead creature. You must also seek out and put to rest any mindless or destructive undead creatures you come across.

You’ve sworn a pact with a powerful fey creature that longs to see the wonders of the Universe. You gain the Fey Jump ability. In exchange, you can no longer see the moon or stars as the fey steals those wonders from your eyes, and you must gaze at the empty sky for at least 10 minutes each night. If you do not, the fey revokes your benefits for the next day. If you go a week without gazing, the fey revokes your benefits until you atone. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Fey Jump;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) You jump through the First World for a brief second, teleporting up 60 feet away to an empty space you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you’re carrying it in an extradimensional container—the action is lost.

You've sworn a pact with a powerful [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83)—typically an olethros advocate or [yamaraj](/Monsters.aspx?ID=770) judge—granting you a reprieve before your soul will be collected in exchange for respect for the dead and assistance against the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). As long as you keep your end of the bargain, you live twice as long as you normally would before dying of natural causes. Additionally, the first time each day that you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points and gain the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) condition, you instead regain a number of Hit Points equal to twice your level (starting from 0 HP), remain conscious, and gain [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) equal to your level for 3 rounds.

 In exchange, you swear to treat the dead you come across with respect, performing last rites and final dispositions to ensure their spirits rest in peace and are less likely to rise as undead. Furthermore, you swear to destroy undead you come across, so long as it's within your power to do so without inordinate risk to yourself. Violating your part of the pact causes its protections to immediately end. If at that point you had already lived beyond your natural lifespan, the psychopomps typically give you a few moments to make any last farewells, and then you simply breathe your final breath and pass on.

You've sworn a pact with Jenway Nightblossom of the Synod of Truth in Dreams, a talented oneiromancer and pactbinder. Through your connection to her, you're able to divine your dreams for wisdom, and they're protected from interference. You're immune to [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1615). During your daily preparations, if you slept and were able to dream, you learn a helpful piece of advice about your future activities, as [_read omens_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1647).

 As payment, Jenway established a permanent telepathic connection to you that functions whenever you sleep or dream. Whenever you learn something significant, Jenway learns it the next time you sleep. You can withhold information, but you lose the benefits of Pact of the Nightblossom until you relent and allow Jenway to learn it.

While the students of Cobyslarni are taught to make pacts with many kinds of dragons, a pact with a rune dragon is somewhat more frequent due to their interest in the accomplishments of various academies. You immediately learn 10 languages chosen from common languages, uncommon languages, and any others the dragon has access to. Additionally, you can [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) at a range of 30 feet as a single action ability with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait.

If you fail to send an appropriately detailed report, you lose this ability unless you spend one week serving the dragon.

>
[Pactbinder Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3822) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 166

**Archetype** [Pactbinder](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=189)

**Prerequisites**
trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) as well as either [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

The first step toward forming a successful pact is an understanding of the magic behind it, along with skill at negotiation. It doesn't hurt that you also learned how to magically bind yourself to keep your word, enabling you to bargain more easily. You increase your proficiency from trained to expert in Diplomacy and in one of the following: Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion.

 **Binding Vow** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You bind yourself by formally speaking a binding vow. Supernatural power flows through and around you as you speak it, and all those present to hear it intrinsically know that it binds you. Breaking this vow is anathema to you, and if you break it willingly, you lose all pactbinder benefits until you fulfill your vow or, if that's impossible, participate in an atone ritual. The vow doesn't prevent unwilling violations and can't be used to try to circumvent mind-control magic, [confusion](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5), or similar situations where you perform an action not entirely of your own volition. A Binding Vow doesn't end until you've fulfilled it. Even if you die, the vow still binds you if you return to life. The vow doesn't force you to go to ridiculous extremes, such as dying, to fulfill your vow unless you specifically swear to go to such extremes. Trying to subvert your binding vow by making selfish promises (such as swearing to an ally that you'll kill someone you already wanted to kill) is in itself a violation of your vow, as is attempting to subvert other vows you've made (such as those from other pactbinder feats or a champion's code).

 When you make a [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) or [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=52) directly in service of fulfilling your vow, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check against any creatures aware of your vow.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the pactbinder archetype.

</column>

---

The first step toward forming a successful pact is an understanding of the magic behind it, along with skill at negotiation. It doesn't hurt that you also learned how to magically bind yourself to keep your word, enabling you to bargain more easily. You increase your proficiency from trained to expert in Diplomacy and in one of the following: Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion. Many feats from this archetype involve swearing specific pacts. You typically can't retrain out of these feats. You gain the Binding Vow action.

 **Binding Vow** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You bind yourself by formally speaking a binding vow. Supernatural power flows through and around you as you speak it, and all those present to hear it intrinsically know that it binds you. Breaking this vow is anathema to you, and if you break it willingly, you lose all pactbinder benefits until you fulfill your vow or, if that's impossible, participate in an atone ritual. The vow doesn't prevent unwilling violations and can't be used to try to circumvent mind-control magic, confusion, or similar situations where you perform an action not entirely of your own volition. A Binding Vow doesn't end until you've fulfilled it. Even if you die, the vow still binds you if you return to life. The vow doesn't force you to go to ridiculous extremes, such as dying, to fulfill your vow unless you specifically swear to go to such extremes. Trying to subvert your binding vow by making selfish promises (such as swearing to an ally that you'll kill someone you already wanted to kill) is in itself a violation of your vow, as is attempting to subvert other vows you've made (such as those from other pactbinder feats or a champion's sanctification).

 When you make a [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) or [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394) directly in service of fulfilling your vow, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check against any creatures aware of your vow.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Pactbound Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3414) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 10

**Archetype** [Pactbound Initiate](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=167)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10); [Erutaki](/Languages.aspx?ID=54) or [Giant](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) language, must have earned the trust of a saumen kar who initiates you into the archetype

</column>

---

You befriended one of the last saumen kar and were infused with a fraction of their power, granting you the potential to become a guardian of their ancient pact. You gain [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) resistance equal to half your level. You can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) while it's snowing even lightly, even if it wouldn't be thick enough to normally grant [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4). Finally, all saumen kar can sense the mark of their pact upon you, and their attitude toward you is typically one step better than it would be otherwise ([hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) to [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=40), unfriendly to [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25), etc.) Most saumen kar are unfriendly to outsiders; this would make them indifferent to you.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the pactbound initiate archetype.

<title level="2">Pactbound Dedication leads to...</title>
[Crown of the Saumen Kar](/Feats.aspx?ID=3416), [Frostbite Runes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3417), [Ice Crafter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3415)

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />

Sangpotshi practitioners know that suffering is a fleeting sensation that ultimately strengthens the soul and prepares it for a new reincarnation. Bolstered by this understanding, you've learned to temporarily steel yourself against all forms of pain. You gain resistance 10 to all damage until the end of your next turn.

    right="Feat 6"

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powderkeg](/Sources.aspx?ID=119) pg. 79

**Prerequisites**
expert in Fortitude saves

**Access**
You're from Alkenstar or the Mana Wastes.

</column>

---

You gain resistance to mental damage equal to half your level and a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects that would make you [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), or [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13). 

<title level="2">Black Powder Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powderkeg](/Sources.aspx?ID=119) pg. 55

If the characters agree to Nixbrix's challenge to defeat Bitey or otherwise impress the gang leader, he offers to teach them a few tricks. The characters gain access to the feats in the Black-Powder Berserkers section on page 79, even if they aren't from Alkenstar or the Mana Wastes, though they still must meet the feats' other prerequisites to take them.

**Related Feats**: [Black Powder Flash](/Feats.aspx?ID=3572), [Inured to Alchemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=3573), [Powder Punch Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3575), [Thunder Clap](/Feats.aspx?ID=3576)

<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 44

</column>

---

You break a trinket such as a lodestone or jade pendant in two, creating a sympathetic link between the halves that bridges distance. During your daily preparations, you perform a short ceremony where you gift one of the two halves to a willing ally. On that ally, you can cast spells and use thaumaturge abilities that have a range of touch at a range of 30 feet instead, and the ally can cast spells that have a range of touch on you from a range of 30 feet. These effects last as long as you and the ally have their half; if either half leaves either of your possession for even a moment, or if you establish a link with a new ally during your next daily preparations, the link breaks.

[Paired Shots](/Feats.aspx?ID=3168) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 112

**Requirements**
You're wielding two weapons, each of which can be either a loaded one-handed firearm or loaded one-handed crossbow.

</column>

---

Your shots hit simultaneously. Make two Strikes, one with each of your two ranged weapons, each using your current multiple attack penalty. Both Strikes must have the same target. 

If both attacks hit, combine their damage and then add any applicable effects from both weapons. You add any precision damage, only once, to the attack of your choice. Combine the damage from both Strikes and apply resistances and weaknesses only once. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

</title>

<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 288

**Archetype** [Palatine Detective](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=306)

**Prerequisites**
[investigator](/Classes.aspx?ID=59)

</column>

---

You have delved into the study of the occult and divine, becoming exceptionally skilled at identifying when such forces are at work. Using this esoteric knowledge and your own ingenuity, you have crafted a small charm that soothes your mind and protects you against harm. This charm usually takes the form of a silver chain, a golden scarab, or a withered hand. While you wear this charm, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against mental effects. In addition, you gain the Mystic Aegis reaction. 

 **Mystic Aegis** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Trigger** A creature you have successfully [Recalled Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about would damage you; **Requirements** You have a free hand; **Effect** You brandish your charm, channeling and shaping the forces within it to protect you against harm. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to all damage equal to 2 + half your level rounded up against the triggering effect.

<title level="2">Palatine Detective Dedication leads to...</title>
[Challenge Insight](/Feats.aspx?ID=7562), [Cursebreaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=7563), [Esoteric Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=7558), [Open the Blazing Eye](/Feats.aspx?ID=7565), [Palatine Enchantment](/Feats.aspx?ID=7560), [Palatine Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7561), [Text Decoder](/Feats.aspx?ID=7559)

---

Your mount becomes a grotesque creature of foreboding when you ride it. Its appearance transforms as flames erupt from its skin, a whorl of negative energy surrounds it, or poison leaks from its flesh. When you Mount your steed ally, you can choose fire, negative, or poison. As long as you ride it, your steed gains resistance 10 to the chosen damage type, and any creature that touches your steed takes 1d6 damage of the chosen type; this includes hitting the steed with unarmed attacks or with a melee weapon Strike while adjacent to the steed. This damage increases to 2d6 at 16th level and 3d6 at 20th level.

You can make yourself as flat as a paper doll or shadow. You can spend 1 minute in motionless meditation before performing an odd step that takes you partially out of this plane, leaving your body completely flat. In this state, you can slip under doors, through tiny cracks, or anywhere a single sheet of paper could, but you can’t cast spells, activate items, or use actions that have the [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540) or [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) traits. You remain in this state for 1 minute unless you choose to return to normal sooner as an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait.

---

You unleash the pent-up chaos within you, becoming a nexus of unbridled destruction that wreaks unfettered havoc on everyone in your vicinity. Each creature within 15 feet of you takes 14d6 acid, electricity, or sonic damage, chosen randomly for each target. Each target receives a basic Reflex save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC, but any creature that is subjected to the type of damage for which you currently have resistance through your Proteankin lineage takes a –2 penalty to the save. Any target that critically fails the save is also confused until the end of their next turn.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Paragon Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=2171) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 72

**Archetype** [Pure Legion Enforcer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=377) (Level 7)

**Prerequisites**
[Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=760); Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9)

</column>

---

Kassi Aziril taught you her techniques that originated the modern use of [Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=760). When you successfully use Battle Medicine, you can also reduce the target's [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), or [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) condition by 1 (this has no effect if you are subject to an effect continually applying the clumsy condition, like [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=102)). If you are legendary in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9), you can choose to reduce the target's [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) condition by 1 instead, and if you have the [Godless Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=869) feat, you can choose to reduce the target's [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) or [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) condition by 1 instead. If you have the [Mortal Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=1181) feat, you can reduce all available conditions by 1 for a target who hasn't benefited from positive or healing magic in the last 24 hours, and if you roll a critical success before applying the effects of the feat, you reduce all available conditions by 2 for that target instead.

<title level="2">Kassi's Techniques</title>

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 71

While Kassi shares her greatest discoveries with the entire medical community, some of her techniques are either still experimental or extremely difficult to perform. Any students who Kassi takes on gain access to her techniques.

**Related Feats**: [Medical Researcher](/Feats.aspx?ID=2170)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Parallel Breakthrough](/Feats.aspx?ID=3669) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 25

</column>

---

You expand your mind beyond your area of psychic specialty. You gain a 1st-level psi cantrip for a conscious mind other than your own; this can be either the unique surface cantrip or one of the common cantrips and the accompanying amp. If you choose a common cantrip, you also gain the special benefit granted by that conscious mind when casting the cantrip without an amp. You don't gain any other benefits of that conscious mind, such as additional spells known.

>
[Paralyzing Slash](/Feats.aspx?ID=3509) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Incapacitation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=93" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 49

**Archetype** [Ghoul](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=178)

**Prerequisites**
[Feverish Enzymes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3507)

</column>

---

Your enzymes can paralyze your foes rather than merely making it harder for them to heal their wounds. Strike with your claw or jaws. If you hit a living non-[elf](/Traits.aspx?ID=58) creature, it becomes [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28) unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Regardless of the result of the save, the creature is temporarily immune to Paralyzing Slash for 24 hours. A creature that becomes paralyzed can attempt a new save to end the paralysis at the end of each of its turns, and the DC cumulatively decreases by 1 on each such save.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Parthenogenic Hatchling](/Feats.aspx?ID=1052) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lizardfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=226" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 58

</column>

---

You were hatched from an unfertilized egg during hard times for your people, and you are a biological copy of your mother. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against diseases. Each of your successful saving throws against a disease reduces its stage by 2, or by 1 for a virulent disease. Each critical success against an ongoing disease reduces its stage by 3, or by 2 for a virulent disease. You take damage only every 2 hours from thirst and every 2 days from starvation, rather than every hour and every day.

**Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 167

**Archetypes** [Dandy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=55), [Venture-Gossip](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=311) (Level 7)

**Prerequisites**
[Dandy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1935); Master in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14)

</column>

---

You attend all the fashionable society parties, no matter how exclusive they might be. Any time you encounter a social event you would ordinarily be denied access to, such as a coronation, royal gala, or other society function, you can spend 1d4 hours to secure entry without the need for a skill check. You find invitations, invitees looking for fashionable dates, temporary jobs with the caterers, event staff willing to look the other way, or some other mode of access for yourself and your allies. This ability doesn't apply to secret events or other small private gatherings with no staff, dates, or outsiders involved.

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 47 **Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Prerequisites** [Ghost Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3496); Master in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) --- Filtering your form through the substance of an object, you can pass through walls, doors, and more. You Fly up to your Speed. During this movement, you can try to move through one object. Attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check as you try to enter its space. The DC is typically 30 to move through a wall of up to 5 feet, 15 for an ordinary door, and 10 for thinner structures like windows; the GM might set the DC higher for especially dense materials like [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=271) or lead, or for barriers that are magically reinforced. You can't Pass Through an obstacle made of magical force, such as a [_wall of force_](/Spells.aspx?ID=363). **Success** You move through the object, treating the square within it as difficult terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, you can move out of it only if you Pass Through again or use some other means of moving through a solid object. As normal for being [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222), starting your turn inside an object makes you [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for that turn.
**Failure** Your movement ends, and you trigger reactions as if you moved out of the square you started in.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs=""
>
[Pass Vengeful Judgement](/Feats.aspx?ID=7399) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Sanctified" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=519" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 132

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392)

**Requirements**
Your hierophant invoked your judgment on their previous turn

</column>

---

To prevent yourself from frivolously calling down the terrible power of divine wrath, you have vowed to do so only with the assent of your mortal hierophant. If your hierophant successfully Strikes a target, they can spend a single action to invoke your wrath. On your turn, you can then Pass Vengeful Judgment on the target, calling down a scouring pillar of divine energy that deals 20d10 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage with a basic Fortitude save. You do not need to have line of effect to the target and it functions at any range. If one of your current domain spells can deal a type of damage other than spirit, you can choose to match this damage type (for instance, calling down a flaming pillar that deals [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) damage if you have the [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76) domain).

If you spend a Mythic Point as part of Passing your Vengeful Judgment, the blast extends into the heavens, scattering the clouds in a detonation visible to all creatures within a 10-mile radius as a show of wrath and a warning to those who would dare harm your followers or question your commandments. For the next month, you and your hierophant gain a +2 status bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks against creatures in the area.

**Special** If you have [Font of Life or Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=7397) , you can choose for the damage type to be [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) (if you chose heal) or [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) (if you chose harm) when you use this ability.

Your Pathfinder training has broadened your horizons and made you more flexible at various skills, since you never know when you might need an obscure skill to complete your mission. You become trained in one skill of your choice, or expert in a skill of your choice in which you were trained. You also become trained in Pathfinder [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8), or an expert if you were already trained. When using a skill untrained, your proficiency bonus is equal to your level instead of 0. You gain access to [_wayfinders_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=470).

You have fully realized the ability to serve as a patron. 

Your newfound abilities enhance your senses, rolling back the veil of a realm hidden to most mortals where great beings vie for unimaginable influence over vast worlds. You gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2410), constant [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727), and the ability to see into all other transitive planes that overlap the one you are in. 

You can be a patron for other witches. Choose a single type of patron you represent, such as [The Resentment](/Patrons.aspx?ID=14) or [Starless Shadow](/Patrons.aspx?ID=17). An allied witch you can observe who has that patron counts as and gains the benefits of your [Witch’s Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=5003) feat, even if you did not select them as your charge during your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575).

You learn the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual and can impart that knowledge to your charges. Once per month, when one of your charges performs the _wish_ ritual, you can roll the skill check in their place.

Your patron partially manifests itself through your familiar to claim a foe’s power for its own. Your familiar gains the following activity.

**Patron’s Claim** <actions string="Two Actions" /> **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** Your familiar’s mouth opens impossibly wide before your patron’s grasping limb stretches forth from it at a creature within 30 feet, dealing 10d10 spirit damage with a basic Fortitude save against your spell DC. Your patron can direct its attention through your familiar, and its mere presence becomes an ominous weight on the minds of other beings to distract them and blot out their magic. Your familiar gains the following activity.

**Patron’s Presence** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (aura) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** A palpable weight extends from your familiar in a 15-foot emanation. Enemies who enter or start their turn within the aura must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC or become stupefied 2 as long as they remain within the aura, or stupefied 3 on a critical failure. The aura lasts until the end of your next turn, but the familiar can Sustain it up to 1 minute.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Chelaxian Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=384)

**Prerequisites**
[Chelaxian Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8971)

**Trigger**
An ally within 30 feet of you critically succeeds at an attack roll or skill check.

</column>

---

A true aristocrat knows how to encourage their best hirelings, ensuring loyalty and future excellence. You praise the triggering ally, granting them one of the following benefits. The ally is then immune to this ability for 1 day. 

**Eagerness:** Invigorated by praise, the ally can [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=1434), [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) with a nearby object, [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), [Reload](/Rules.aspx?ID=2196), or [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) as a reaction. 

**Persistence:** For 1 minute, the ally gains [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) equal to half your level plus your Charisma modifier. 

**Validation:** If the ally has the [panache class feature](/Classes.aspx?ID=63), they gain panache.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Limited"
>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #163: Ruins of Gauntlight](/Sources.aspx?ID=71) pg. 81

**Archetype** [Ghost Hunter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=88)

**Prerequisites**
[Ghost Hunter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2277)

</column>

---

You have uncanny insight into the way [ghosts](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51) and [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) manifest, manipulate the mind, and rejuvenate. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects caused by [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and haunts, and you can roll a [Spirit Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Haunt Lore check for initiative if you know that an incorporeal undead or a haunt is present.

If you are present when a spirit or haunt is defeated, you instantly gain a flash of insight into how it can be permanently put to rest. Typically, this flash manifests as a vision that presents a quick scene closely linked to the source of the spirit or haunt's creation. Attempt a Spirit Lore or Haunt Lore check, respectively, with a DC appropriate for the spirit or haunt's level. On a success, you gain a hint about how to put the spirit to rest or permanently disable the haunt; on a critical success, you learn the exact method of doing so.

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 35 **Prerequisites** [Battle-Hardened Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7815) --- As veterans of countless battles, you and your companion share an indomitable strength. The companion you gained with [Commander's Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7793) is now a [specialized animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2120). You can select one of the usual specializations or the peerless mascot specialization. A commander's companion with the peerless mascot specialization gains the following benefits.
  • It gains a 30-foot aura that grants the same benefits as your banner, effectively acting as a second banner. If you have your actual banner affixed to your companion, the aura is a single 60-foot aura (this includes the increased aura benefit from [Battle-Tested Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7808)). If you later gain the [Glorious Banner](/Feats.aspx?ID=7829) feat, your banner has a 100-foot aura while it is affixed to your peerless mascot companion.
  • It gains the beast trait.
  • Its Intelligence modifier increases by 2 and its Wisdom modifier increases by 1.
  • It is an expert in Warfare Lore. It can speak one language that you also speak (chosen at the time you gain this feat).
  • Its maximum Hit Points increase by 20, increasing to 25 at 18th level, and 30 at 20th level.
  • Its mastery of all kinds of battlefields grants it a climb Speed and swim Speed equal to its land Speed; if it already had a Speed that was greater than its land Speed, then it has a climb Speed, swim Speed, and land Speed that are all equal to the highest Speed it has.

    pfs="Standard"

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 177

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You use clever tactics to mislead your foes as you sneak away. You Sneak while leaving a decoy behind. The decoy acts as the spell [_mislead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1605), though you aren’t invisible, just undetected. You can continue to concentrate to move your decoy, as with the spell, whether or not you remain hidden throughout the duration. Once you use Perfect Distraction, you need to spend 10 minutes to set up another decoy before you can use it again.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 290

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566)

</column>

---

Your knowledge of Razmir’s faith and doctrines has grown. You excel in debating priests of rival faiths, wielding truths as subtly and deftly as any charlatan might wield a lie. When you use [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389), you can carefully structure your deceits so that each individual statement you make is the truth, from a certain perspective. As long as you are wearing your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3592), you don’t take a penalty to Deception checks while subject to the [_ring of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1656) spell or similar effects. Whenever you are subject to _ring of truth_ or a similar effect, you can attempt a Deception check when you first begin speaking to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the spell’s effects, with a counteract rank equal to half your level (rounded up); succeeding at this check doesn’t end the spell or effect, but it does cause it to indicate that you are speaking the truth, even when you are actually lying, as you weave a web of words so delicate that even you can’t be certain where the truth ends and deception begins.

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42); Expert in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45)

</column>

---

With your experience as a performer, you can keep a set of medical tools handy at all times. You can wear a [healer's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727) as part of any costume or disguise. Creatures will generally only notice the toolkit it if they use a [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action and succeed at a Perception check against your Performance DC.

 In addition, you can realize at the last moment when you should just be pretending to avoid doing any lasting harm. When you critically fail a Medicine check to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396), [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=2397), [Treat Poison](/Actions.aspx?ID=2398), or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399), you can attempt a Performance check against the patient’s Perception DC. On a success, your critical failure at the Medicine check becomes a failure.

You developed techniques for discovering a target’s weaknesses to poisons using your forensic knowledge. When you study a location that a creature spends a lot of time in, such as a bedroom or office, you learn medical conditions, reactions, or sensitivities that make them susceptible to poisons. Subsequently, whenever you craft an [alchemical poison](/Rules.aspx?ID=3185), you can tailor it to a creature you have studied in this way, giving that creature a –2 circumstance penalty to Fortitude saves against the poison and giving other creatures a +2 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves against it.

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Pesh Skin](/Feats.aspx?ID=1152) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=52" />
<trait label="Morph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=113" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #149: Against the Scarlet Triad](/Sources.aspx?ID=14) pg. 78

**Requirements**
You are transformed into a plant by a polymorph spell.

</column>

---

Your plant form sprouts hundreds of spines, and your blood causes mild hallucinations in creatures exposed to it. Each time a creature touches you, hits you with an unarmed attack, or hits you with a melee weapon attack while adjacent to you, that creature takes 1d6 piercing damage. Increase the damage to 2d6 if the polymorph spell is 8th level or higher, or to 3d6 if it’s 10th level.

 When an adjacent creature damages you with piercing or slashing damage, it must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or become [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) (or stupefied 2 on a critical failure) until the end of its next turn.

 These benefits last until you’re no longer polymorphed into a plant.

<title level="2">Katapesh Poisoners</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #149: Against the Scarlet Triad](/Sources.aspx?ID=14) pg. 78

Famous not only for its pesh cash crop and the host of medicinal plants that grow naturally in the nearby desert, but also for the consistent demand for efficient toxins, Katapesh has developed its own specialized poisons and toxic techniques. The city's infamous Poison Maker's Guild is the source of many of these concoctions as well as secret techniques for using them, though unscrupulous Katapeshi bodyguards, thieves, and assassins all know at least one poison recipe or a unique means of inflicting such toxins.

**Related Feats**: [Deadly Poison Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=1151), [Shaped Contaminant](/Feats.aspx?ID=1153)

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 259 --- You have a pet-a Tiny animal of a type you choose, such as a cat, bird, or rodent. It has the minion trait, meaning it gains 2 actions during your turn if you use the [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) action to command it; this replaces the usual effects of Command an Animal, and you don't need to attempt a Nature check. A pet can't take [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540) actions except to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) or [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375). **Level** Your pet's level is equal to yours. **Modifiers and AC** Your pet's save modifiers and AC are equal to yours before applying circumstance or status bonuses or penalties. It uses 3 + your level as its modifier for Perception, Acrobatics, and Stealth, and just your level as its modifier for other skill checks. It doesn't have or use its own attribute modifiers and can never benefit from item bonuses. **Hit Points** Your pet has 5 Hit Points per level. **Senses** Your pet has low-light vision and can gain additional senses from pet abilities. **Speed** Your pet has a Speed of 25 feet. You can choose to instead have an aquatic pet, which breathes in water instead of air and has the aquatic trait, no land Speed, and a swim Speed of 25 feet. **Pet Abilities** When you gain your pet, choose two of the following abilities. If your pet is an animal that naturally has one of these abilities (for instance, an owl has a fly Speed), you must select that ability. Your pet can't be an animal that naturally has more pet abilities than the maximum. In some cases, the GM might add some familiar abilities described on pages 212–213 to the pet abilities you can choose.
  • **Amphibious** It gains the amphibious trait, allowing it to breathe in both air and water, and has both a land Speed and a swim Speed, each equal to its highest land Speed or swim Speed.
  • **Burrower** It gains a burrow Speed of 5 feet, allowing it to dig Tiny holes.
  • **Climber** It gains a climb Speed of 25 feet.
  • **Darkvision** It gains darkvision.
  • **Echolocation** Your pet can use hearing as a precise sense within 20 feet.
  • **Fast Movement** Increase one of the pet's Speeds from 25 feet to 40 feet.
  • **Flier** It gains a fly Speed of 25 feet.
  • **Manual Dexterity** It can use up to two of its limbs as if they were hands to perform manipulate actions.
  • **Scent** Your pet can use scent as an imprecise sense within 30 feet
  • **Tough** Your pet's max HP increase by 2 per level.
**Special** You can replace a pet or gain a new one by spending 1 week of downtime, releasing any previous pet you have. If you later gain a familiar or other companion that uses the Pet feat, you can immediately retrain this feat. Pet leads to... [Ferocious Beasts](/Feats.aspx?ID=4527), [GGGHhhjjjJJK](/Feats.aspx?ID=8804)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Petrified Skin](/Feats.aspx?ID=3756) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 56

**Prerequisites**
You have been [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=30) by an enemy.

</column>

---

It might have been a [medusa](/Monsters.aspx?ID=297), [dracolisk](/Monsters.aspx?ID=565), or even a [fossil golem](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1174); regardless of the source, you were the target of some petrifying effect, and an element of that stony gaze has remained with you, both protecting and slowly consuming you. Your limbs are coated with a layer of stone that rests atop your skin and covers more of your body as you lose health. You gain a stone fist [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d8 bludgeoning damage, has the [shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) trait, and is in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapon group (unlike a normal fist, it doesn't have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) or [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) traits).

 Additionally, you become more petrified as your life force ebbs. When you have fewer than half your maximum Hit Points, you increase the damage die size of your stone fist from 1d8 to 1d10 and gain resistance to physical damage (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374)) equal to your Constitution modifier.

 If you would gain the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) condition, you can choose to instead be permanently petrified and avoid the risk of death. When you do, you enter your petrified form with your full maximum Hit Points instead of the normal number. If you become unpetrified, you return to 0 Hit Points, as normal. You can't voluntarily end this petrification. [Counteracting](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) this petrification requires a casting of [_stone to flesh_](/Spells.aspx?ID=311) of a spell level equal to at least half your level, and a successful counteract check against the hard DC for your level. Other effects like _stone to flesh_ have similar limitations, as determined by the GM. Each time you recover from this petrification, you gain a new scar on your skin in the shape of a long, thin crack.
